video_title: Motivational Interviewing: Evoking Commitment to Change

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, John. Nice to see you again. So, tell me, how are things going?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, doc, I know you told me that I need to lose weight. And even though the scale didn't show today, I was able to lose about 5 pounds, but then I gained it right back.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate you bringing your weight to the forefront. Do you mind if we explore this issue further?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, by all means. I know we have to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right. Uh, well, it sounds like you've been struggling with your weight recently. And I understand how difficult it is to lose the weight and then have it come back again. So, tell me what you did to lose that initial 5 pounds.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I started watching what I ate and I ate less. I've been eating more fruits and vegetables. I've also been walking a lot. I'm walking up to 20 minutes a day now. I saw the weight come slowly off, um, and I felt better. But then when I watched it come back on again, you know, I gave up.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: But you did have some success. Tell me how you felt when you lost the weight.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I felt great and I felt really proud of myself. I thought that this was something that I could do.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it sounds like you realized that when you lost the weight you feel better and that it's gonna affect your overall health. So, tell me what you think changed that caused you to gain the weight back.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I think it's because I've been eating more fruits and vegetables, that- that's it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And how many servings of fruits and vegetables on average per day would you have?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: To be honest, I have four or five -- four to six glasses of orange juice a day. Um, I have fruit for lunch and breakfast. I have, uh, usually one to two servings of a vegetable like lettuce or broccoli with thinner.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: John, it's very important that you recognize that some fruits, but especially fruit juice can contain a huge amount of calories. Did you know that a glass of orange juice has almost as many calories as a can of cola?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, I didn't know. Um, but doesn't the fruit- food pyramid classify, um, fruit juice as a- a serving?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, but keep in mind that the food pyramid is to be used as a guideline only. When it comes to nutrition, we have to have a more personalized approach. So I have a hunch, and that is the excess fruit that you were consuming probably caused your weight rebound. What's your impression?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, this changes quite a bit. I mean, here I'm thinking that my fruit intake is making me healthier and actually it's making me fatter.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Indeed. Let me ask you something, knowing what you know now, how important is it to you to lose the weight by decreasing the amount of juice that you're currently taking in?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Obviously, I need to cut back on the fruit juice. But boy, do I love that OJ.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, I understand. Let me ask you this, on a scale from 0 to 10, 0 meaning that there's no way you can do it, and 10 meaning that you're 100% confident that you can do it, how confident are you that you'll be able to reduce the amount of juice you're currently taking in.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, six or seven.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right. So, you're not a zero. So, that tells me that you've got some confidence that this is doable, this is something you certainly can do it. Why are you not a zero?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I guess it's because I know that I need to do it to lose the weight.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you realize, again, that if you decrease the amount of juice you're taking in, you're gonna decrease your weight, you're gonna feel better, and you're gonna impact your po- health positively?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: But you're also not a 10, and that tells me that there may be some obstacles to your success. What would it take for you to be a 10 or even an 8 or 9?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Getting the fruit juice of the house because I know if it's there I'll drink it. My wife does the shopping for us, so maybe if I ask her not to get the juice, that would solve it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if the juice was still there, can you think of anything else you could do?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I suppose I could replace it with, um, a low-calorie drink or drink more water.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Excellent. John, I get the impression that you want to stay in course with weight reduction. And the best way to do this will be to decrease the amount of juice that you're currently taking in. So if I saw you in two weeks and I asked you how much juice you're t- drinking and how you did it, what would you tell me?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'd say I didn't have any and I substituted it with, um, sugar-free drinks.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Excellent. Well, it sounds like you have a plan. Same scale, 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can, uh, make this happen?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I agree. All right. Well, you-you know what? I'm not gonna start any medications today. Your levels were a little bit off, but I think we can handle this from a purely lifestyle standpoint. What do you think?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Great. It sounds good to me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Excellent. I'll see you in two weeks.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: Yeah. Mm. How would you like it to be?

utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.text: Okay, so asthma is one.

utterances.text: What else?

video_title: Dr. Marilyn Herie -- MI Skills -- Tobacco Cessation -- Angry Client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, what brings you here, Bob? What's, what can I do to help?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah, well, the only reason I'm here is 'cause my wife thinks I've got a problem with smoking. I've been smoking all my life and, uh, six months ago, uh, she thought, she got into this health kick, right? And now everyone who smokes is evil. And, uh, so that's why I'm here just to please her, get her off my back and—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you're not too happy to be here. This is the last thing that you want to be doing this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. That's an understatement. I mean, I'm supposed to be at work right now, too, right? So-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You've taken time off you, it's costing you time and money being here.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. I'm only here because my wife forced me to come, you know. Like this has come to a head six months of just nagging me, relentless every day, because she was able to quit smoking and now I have to quit.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, let me ask you this, Bob, what are some of your wife's concerns about your smoking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, she's concerned about my health and she cuts out all these articles from the paper about second-hand smoke and—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Wow, that she's been showing you and making you read.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I've got to read this. That's my reading assignment for breakfast and I want to go out and have-- We used to go out and have a cigarette together at the table. Now I have to go outside in this weather, you know, what's that about? And she used to smoke more than me and now she's like holier than now?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you're pretty angry about it. It's pretty outraging that you're forced to change your whole life because of a decision she made six months ago.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And she's got my kids on this against me, you know, my son and my daughter, they're, it's like, they're ganging up on me, you know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, from your perspective, do you see any consequences to your smoking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, the big one of course is how it's affecting my wife and the family. Like my dad's 85, he still smokes. I mean, yeah, you know, sometimes I thought of quitting, but I mean, I don't know. I don't know if I can-- I don't know if I can quit.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, let me make sure I understand kind of the whole scenario 'cause there's a lot of pieces to it. Your wife is on your case and your kids are ganging up too. So, you're sort of isolated, you're put in a corner and you're being told this is something you have to do, you have no choice in the matter.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You have a few concerns about your health, but that's not really the driving force. It sounds like it's most of all that it would be nice if things just went back to the way they were before she quit smoking and that all of this stuff wasn't something that you had to deal with anymore. Does that pretty much sum up--?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. I-I'm just, I don't want to lose her or my family over smoking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I get the feeling that your relationship is really important to you. That you would do anything.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I mean, we've been married over 25 years, and uh, we've never had any major problems. Like this is-- this is the first problem. I don't even really see it as a problem cause we used to both smoke and I was trying to accommodate them by smoking outside, but it's feeling like we're going like this and I'm just concerned, like if this keeps going, like.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, it strikes me that the way that we're talking about it, it's like it's all or nothing. Either you keep smoking the way you are, things continue to go downhill and get worse, your wife gets more and more on your case, or you put your cigarettes down starting the moment you walk in the door tonight and never pick them up again. It's almost like one or the other. It strikes me that as well there might be some middle ground here that it took you a long time to learn how to be a smoker and maybe it's going to take some time to learn how to stop smoking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, I can actually do it that way like gradual taber?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: There are some medications and some different approaches that we can use that aren't so abrupt. Recognizing that it-it's going to take some time and practice to get to where you might want to be.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I wish my wife could have come today cause she's feels after like, just stop like right away. So do you think she could come with me at a future appointment or something and she could hear that message?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: If you wanted to bring your wife along, I'd be more than happy to talk with both of you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay. I'll have to talk to her as well because their schedule changes from week to week, she works shifts, so I'll call you back tomorrow and we'll set something up.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. That sounds good.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Thanks for coming in.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sarah, I'm so glad you came in for your well-woman exam today. I think we addressed a lot of your concerns. However, I would like to ask you more about your smoking. Would that be okay?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I guess.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So about how much are you smoking over the course of a day? You had said it had increased over once or twice a day.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, um, normally, I'm smoking, you know, like once in the morning, uh, once during my lunch break and then in the evening maybe like five or six.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So about eight cigarettes. So over the course of a day, just under half a pack?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And that's changed over what period of time?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, honestly, it's probably been over the past year or so that I- I've been smoking a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So over the past year, the smoking has increased. And that's been mainly in the evening?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Um, I have a two-year-old son as I mentioned, so I try to never smoke around him. So I'm normally kinda waiting until he gets to bed.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Well, that's the time when you can relax and unwind.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, exactly. You know, I told you, my-my schedule is kinda crazy right now. I, um, I work full-time and I just started back at night classes. So, you know, all that combined, you know, I enjoy that time to myself in the evening.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sure. Sure. Well, it's a time to relax and you've got a lot going on.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So are there other things you do in the evening to relax?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I mean, maybe I'll have like a drink or two.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. A drink or two. So about how many drinks would you say you have over the course of a day?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, maybe like two max.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Two max. How many drinks would you say you'd have over the course of a week?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, I don't really get why you're asking me that. I mean, I just came here, you know, for a regular visit. I-I am not here to talk about my drinking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: No, I understand- I understand. And I'm certainly not here to tell you what to-to do, Sarah. I'm interested in hearing your thoughts and sharing some information with you, and what you do with that information is totally up to you. You've got a lot going on. You're a mother, you're working, you're going to school, and our healthcare team wants to make sure that you have all the resources available to you to meet your goals, including good health. And my job as your healthcare provider is to listen to you and to share information with you, including healthcare concerns associated with smoking and alcohol. Would that be okay with you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I guess.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we do know that an increase in smoking and alcohol is associated with certain kinds of cancer; colon cancer, cervical cancer, breast cancer, lung cancer, and, um, also pancreatic cancer. It's also associated with liver and lung disease as well as heart disease, diabetes, and hypertension. So that's a lot of information, but I'm-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -interested in what your thoughts are, Sarah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I-I'm just kinda surprised because, I mean, I don't smoke or drink that much. And I mean, compared to people I work with, you know, I-I smoke a lot less, and I feel like I've actually been trying to keep it pretty low.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you're consciously trying to cut back.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I have a readiness ruler in my pocket here, 0 means not ready to stop smoking at all and 10 means absolutely ready to stop smoking. Where do you see yourself on that scale?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, maybe like a five.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: About a five. So you're halfway there. So why did you choose a five rather than a four?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I mean, you brought up some kinda scary stuff like, you know, cancer risk or other things like that. And you know, being a mother, I-I don't want something to happen to me obviously.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's a lot of information to think about. utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: Okay, great. Let's quantify that a little bit. So how many cigarettes would that be?

utterances.text: Well, right now, if I'm having like five or six, I could try to smoke three in the evening plus, you know, still the couple during the day.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So you-- that's cutting back quite a bit. That's a big step. So since we're kind of running out of time here today, I'm wondering if we could-- would be willing to come back in about four weeks to review this plan?

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: Okay. Can you expand on that a little bit more? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, I don't think I would be, you know, drinking as much or going to parties as much if I'm studying for school, or in college, or trying to get in law school and things like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so, the-the alcohol is something that might make it harder to reach your goals?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, so, when you're sort of looking ahead, how often do you think you might be drinking, say, when you get to college?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, maybe less than I am now. I mean, I don't drink much anyway, so-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -maybe, like, one drink every once in a blue moon.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, you sort of have a plan to cut back on-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -your drinking eventually?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: For sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How might that go?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I guess right now I would try to stop in high school, and once I get older, maybe just like, socially once in a while, but not anything big or anything.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, so, you don't feel the need to make any major changes, but you feel like you could make some adjustments that would make it easier or—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Definitely, yeah. That's a good word.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. How important is it to you to make some adjustments to your drinking, on a scale of 1 to 10? Where 1 is not at all important, not something you're thinking about, and 10 is most important thing.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe a five or six.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And why did you say five or six rather than like two or three?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Because, um, it's not something I do not care about at all, but it's not something that's just constantly on my mind that I want to change about myself.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, it is something you have thought about or something.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. Definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And, how confident are you that you could make a change if you decide you wanted to on that same scale?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I'm pretty confident that I can considering that I'm not really an alcohol user per se.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'm not really into that whole scene, so, it's-it's not gonna bedifficult for me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, what number do you think you'd say?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, on a scale of 1 to 10-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -if I can quit or not?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe like an 8 or 9.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, and why'd you say 8 or 9 rather than even like 5 or 6?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Because, like I said, it's not a big part of my life. So, it's not really that difficult

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, kind of keeping that in mind, it sounds like, um, you do have sort of a-a vague plan to make some adjustments in your drinking at some point-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and, it's moderately important to you. It's something you would like to do because you have these big goals for yourself, and you actually feel very confident that you could be successful with it. What sort of goal do you think might be good to set for today?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, probably to stop, maybe next party I go to, not have a drink at all.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Um, do you feel pretty confident that you could just stop completely?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I can just tell my friends-- My pa-- My friends aren't really that pressuring.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's just like outside people that I don't really know that well.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, I could just tell them, "Hey, I don't feel like having a drink today."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What-what might be some benefits of following through with that goal?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, definitely, I'll have like all my senses there and I'll be aware of everything that's going on.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, health concerns, I guess. I know alcohol is bad for your health.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, that would be one.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, it's-- It sounds like you're actually pretty comfortable with setting a goal of not drinking anymore a-at least at the next part? and seeing how it goes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Do you think it would be all right if we met again to kinda check in on how it goes and-and see if it's working out for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, that would be okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right, great. And then, i-it sounds like some of the benefits you're expecting are, um, health benefits-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -having an easier time with achieving your academic and career goals, and just sort of not having to deal with some of the consequences that your peers do.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, very good. Um, is there anything else that you think would be important for me to know?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, how would you, um, advise me to like get maybe my friends to stop drinking?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, that's a great question. So, a lot of times, kids who are trying to cut back, it's harder if their friends are still drinking, and one of the easiest things is trying to have more activities that don't involve alcohol, but-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -of course, that's harder if you're not the one planning. So, some of the things that can be useful if you're at a party say, um, and there's already alcohol there, and there are other kids that maybe aren't your closest friends, um, some of the things that I would recommend since you're interested are, you know, carrying around a different drink that looks like it has alcohol in it. So, you know, even carrying an empty beer bottle or beer can or, you know, if people are having a mixed drink, just having the coke, say-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -without any alcohol mixed into it. Um, often, having anything in your hand is a good barrier for people who are trying to offer you alcohol, because you already have something in your hand-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, that's a good idea.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and it-it kinda, um, prevents them from trying to stuff something else in there. Do you think any of those things might work for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, for sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What about in terms of talking to your friends about it, have you thought about how you might approach with them or is that something else you'd like some tips about, about telling them about your plan to-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -to stop drinking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -I was just planning on telling them that I don't really want to drink anymore. That wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Your friends would be pretty comfortable with that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, at least my closest friends, for sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, great. Any other concerns or questions? Anything else I can help with?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. No, I think I'm okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So then, like I said, um, I'll try and see if we can meet up maybe in a few weeks and see how it's going-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and then, um, if things are going great, then fantastic, and if you run into any stumbling blocks, then we can maybe problem-solve together.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay, great. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That sound okay?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right. Thanks so much.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: Okay. So you'd, you're feeling a little bit anxious about today.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So what other kinds of difficulties that you have been experiencing?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I mean, I'm-I'm a photographer. utterances.text: Okay. So you said that, um, your difficulties are getting in the way of you doing certain things. utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. utterances.text: So I guess, tell me a bit more about what happens then. utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, just makes me feel like an idiot, makes me feel like I just shouldn't even bother trying to do it anymore. utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Can you give me an example of a-a recent situation? Maybe we can focus on that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, like a work situation or just--?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, time when you were maybe doing a job with some people and you felt the social anxiety, you know, that you're describing, you felt that kick in.

utterances.text: Yeah. I was doing a job where it was kind of like a- a Nature issue and I was having to work with a lot of different people. utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, it was, yeah, it was really cool, but I find it- found it really hard to try and focus on that 'cause I was so- I was kind of feeling really anxious and—

utterances.text: So it wasn't what you expected?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So how long ago was that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That was two weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So it was quite recent.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So on that particular day, what were the thoughts that you had in your head when you were in that situation?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just felt really- just really kind of hot. I couldn't really breathe and just felt like I wanted to just get out. utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I can tell you're getting kind of anxious, even just thinking about that day.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So you're describing quite a lot there to me. So you're saying that you, you kind of got hot and sweaty, you said that you- you held the camera.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: W-what was, do you mean you kind of try to hide behind it or?

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: So you're holding the camera very tightly.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: W-why was that? Why was that helpful?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Cause I felt like I was getting really like hot and flushed and I just thought, at least if I can just-- I don't know. utterances.text: Okay. So, okay. So it sounds like you had a lot of thoughts going through your head. Um, you said that you're worried that everyone's looking at you. What other thoughts were there that were in your mind?

utterances.text: They could tell what—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, um, I was trying to wear black so this kind of tries to cover it up and just like a lot of layers, so they can't tell but, I mean, my hands, like, they were so shaken. I was really red and just was-- Just wishing that I just wasn't there.

utterances.text: So, I mean, you've already described it to me a little bit, but if you think about how you looked that day, how'd-how'd you say, how'd you think you looked?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think just very stupid and, like, I think my face was really red. utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hey, can I help you?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm, and I'm sorry, that's not how I mean to come across at all.

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -if you [unintelligible 00:01:34] was gonna make it like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I-I just hear it every day.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And what's been your past experience with smoking? Tell me-- Can you tell me a little bit about kind of how the role it plays in your life, how long you've smoked?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I've smoked for 40 years, since I was 14-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and quit a couple of times, off and on in my 20s, but, you know, it's been consistent. And I can't see myself changing now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No matter what kinda talk I get or what they come up with.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like almost you've tried a lot of things that are out there and it's not something that you're—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not gonna worked for me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and then they fight it, but [sighs] it's my choice-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and I don't like lectures about it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And it really is your choice. You're absolutely right-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -that nobody has the right to tell you what to do. Um, can I ask? If you were to-- Uh, if there was to be a situation where you decided, "I must quit," what-what would that situation be?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hard to tell 'cause I already had open-heart surgery. That didn't do it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Prostate cancer, that didn't do it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know. I just don't really want it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, this is something that you-you-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -have to-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -pretty much see yourself doing for-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, a while, quite a while. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. Well, I really appreciate you being willing to even talk about it. And I get that right now, this is not something that you wanna pursue. Would it be okay if I brought it up in our next visit? 'Cause I-I know that you've said you don't want a lecture, but on the other hand, I am- I am concerned.

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: [unintelligible 00:03:34] options. I had some-- I had my surgeon just go like, "You're- you're--" like, "Why do I even keep you as a patient?"

video_title: Motivational Interviewing: Discussing Alcohol Use With a Pregnant Woman

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Thank you for coming in to see me today, Nina. I'm looking forward to getting to know you a little bit and hearing a little bit about you and what brought you in here today.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, my doctor referred me. He said I had to come because I've- I've been a little irresponsible with this pregnancy. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. He's thinking you were a little irresponsible.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Um, he said that I was drinking too much with it. Um, I-I haven't been a lot, but he said it was still maybe, um, would screw things up.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you're feeling kind of concerned about that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. Like I don't- I don't want to screw anything up with this baby, but, um, yeah, I'm just- I'm scared I already did.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, you're concerned about the consequences, and you really care about your baby, and you want to give your baby the best start you can.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you're wondering a little bit about this time that we're going to spend together.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. He didn't really tell me what to expect. He just said, "Go- go see her as well."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So here you are today and, um, you're sharing that you have been drinking alcohol throughout your pregnancy.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Um, I didn't find out I was pregnant until probably two-ish months in-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and I had already been drinking then. Um, I've been really trying not to, but, you know, weekends come around, and, um, all my friends are kind of partying and stuff, and it's been hard to, like, break that habit.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So, there's this external pressure coming from the people you care about to sort of stay in the scene.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: A little bit. I think if I- if I talk to them, it would be fine, but it's-it's weird, right? Like I'm the only one of my friends that's, like, taking this step and having a kid, and they don't really know how to handle that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Kind of feels like You're between two worlds. In one world, you're preparing to be a mother and bring a baby into this world, and this other world is the world that you've been in for a while where you're kind of having a good time and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -drinking and your friends are-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, like, I'm- I'm still, like, I'm only in my 20s, and-and for everyone else, it's like, "Okay, it's party time," and now I kind of have to, like, break out of that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, this party-time world's- are you feeling like this is something you want to move out of and move into that mom world? Or does it feel like I want to hang out there still too?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: There's, yeah, there's part of me that still wants to live that out because I'm not going to have another chance, like once this kid comes, it's-it's going to be over. I know I'm gonna- I know I'm going to have to change.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, for you, you're feeling like once the baby comes and actually in your arms, then things are going to change, but right now, while you're pregnant, you're thinking, "I can kind of hang out in both worlds a little bit," but part of you may be thinking maybe that's not the case. It's time to go to the mom world maybe.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Probably. And I'm also feeling like it's too late. I already screwed it up.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, you've got a lot of concerns about what's happened to- up until this point, as far as your drinking. What do you know about, um, drinking alcohol throughout pregnancy?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I know, like, they say not to, but I thought because my friends didn't really care, I thought, "Okay. Like maybe-maybe it doesn't matter. Maybe it's just what they tell you." Just like drinking, in general, is bad.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you were thinking because your-your friends weren't pressuring you to stop drinking, that-that it must be okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And then there's this other part of you that's- was thinking maybe it's not okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, like, I should probably have trusted my gut.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, your gut is telling you what? Tell me about that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's telling me that what I'm doing is wrong and it's probably hurting my kid and that- that I'm gonna really regret that once I actually get my kid.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you really wanna do what's best for your babe. And kind of wondering, um, how to move forward from here, is that where you wanna, you know, kind of focus in on, or what are your thoughts about giving up drinking altogether?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I'm definitely it's not-- I think I could probably do it. It's just- it-it comes hard when you're, like, in that moment. You're around your friends and they're drinking and you don't wanna be- you don't wanna be the mom at that moment. You wanna be yourself. You wanna be who you were before.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you kind of have this identity, dual identity going on. I wanna be that person, yet, that person-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And so many people, when they have kids, they just vanish from their friends. And I don't wanna be that person. I don't wanna be that person that just has a kid and they're completely-completely different.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm. So, embraces this life of the picket fence and the, you know, the little house and having the baby in this-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, suburbs. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you don't wanna be that- that- that woman that's just sort of living in this house with the baby carriage, and at the same time, that world's kind of saying it's behind you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I-I guess. Like, I don't wanna- I don't wanna lose my friends because of this. And I don't wanna put pressure on them to change because they're, I mean, they're good people. They're just—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You care about them.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It's just the scene that they're-they're still in because their life maybe hasn't taken that change that your life has made. And so now, you're here and you're not sure. You want the baby, but you're not sure about the suburbs and the picket fence thing. You're not sure—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don’t want that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You don't want that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You want this baby.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you wanna be, um, take care of your baby as the baby's growing.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like, I wanna- I wanna be responsible for this thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You don't wanna let your baby down.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And at the same time, it's hard to let go of the past, but on the other hand, you're thinking, "I don't have a choice. I've got to look this way." Is that kind of what it feels like?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I guess so. I feel like I've already made a choice and already made some bad choices with this.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Nina, I'm wondering, what's your hope for the future? When you think about where you are today, um, what do you hope for when you look ahead?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I-I kept the kid because I wanted-- It was almost like that push, that sign for me to, like, move forward and become like an adult because it's scary, right? Like I-I still feel like a teenager sometimes. And having that push to be a real person is really-- It's a lot of pressure and I-I want to raise this kid well. I don't wanna- I don't wanna let my kid down. I don't wanna, you know, I don't wanna regret choosing to have this kid because I think it's the right time, but I don't wanna- I don't wanna make mistakes that make me realize maybe I'm not ready for this 'cause sometimes it feels like I'm not ready for this.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You put your heart there that the baby is really- it was almost kind of like a sign for you that was saying, "This baby is giving you a kind of a new chance at life, or giving you a plan B," and you guys both get to decide what plan B is gonna look like.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I just guess it's easier said than done though. Like, it's, like, great, I can make all these changes and I can be a completely new person, but it's, like, at the end of the day, I'm still just who I am.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: While this baby's growing in you and you think of all the opportunities that could come out of this, there's a part of you that says, "I'm still that same girl that was drinking and partying," and-and maybe not living the life you wanted to live.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. And I'm just- you know, you can't just one day flick a switch and become a new person.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: While this baby feels like this is your second chance, you're wondering, "Do I deserve that second chance?" And then this other part of you that says, "Why not? It's here and I wanna go for it."

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I guess that voice is just a little more stifled by the other one.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. You got a lot of people around you that are kind of pulling it down, and it's kind of taking you back to the old life. And the baby is a constant reminder that there’s this new life ahead.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, it's gonna be very different when it actually comes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: When you think about, you know, embracing this new life, and taking that different path, turning away from path A and moving into path B, how confident are you that you can take path B and be successful in raising this baby, and letting go with the drinking and the life that you were in-in path A?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think I'm gonna have to be successful. I don't really- I don't have any other choice. Like I have to- I have to take that path.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Tell me more about that, what makes you say, "I have to take that path"? What makes you feel like you need that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Because I need to for my kid. It's- it's gonna be all screwed up if I don't.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: This part of you that says, "I don't have an option to-to-to make this life better," it's wondering, "Do I have the confidence to be able to make that life a reality?" What do you think you need to increase your confidence that you can do this?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know, like, maybe- maybe actually talking to my friends and saying like- or maybe them actually being able to see this kid and go, "Of course, of course, your- your choice makes sense. You--" Maybe it would, you know, give them a wake-up call too if They actually, like, see it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you're thinking that, um, once your friends see you with the baby in your arms that they too will see that there's a different path for them too?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Or at least they'll feel less pressure to be who they want me to be.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm, kind of feel like you're pulled between two worlds there.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: A little bit.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It's not easy to be in that world and also having that constant reminder that the baby is coming and this baby is saying, "I want this better life," and you want to give the baby a better life too. Who can support you, do you think when-when you look around who's in your circle right now, who do you think can support you in moving towards path B?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Definitely my parents, um, and I probably need to, uh, go and meet some other-other people who are maybe, you know, having kids too so that I can see, like how it's done 'cause like, I only have a younger brother who's like not-not even close to that. So I don't really have anyone in my life that I know that's had kids recently. So I-I would like to meet other, you know, young moms out there who, you know, are kind of struggling with the same stuff I am.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And your parents are a support for you and support you from giving up the drinking, the alcohol use, that's something that they would support-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't think they realize, uh, that I'm doing it or how much I'm doing it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And I know that if they found out, they would be really pissed.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That would be a concern for them as well as for you now.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Is that something that, um, maybe you and I could meet again about-and talk about having those conversations with-with the family, maybe having conversations about, you know, the folks, your-your friends that are currently in the lifestyle that you were involved with, um, and then sort of what it would look like to go down path B, is that something that you would be open to meeting with me about again?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think so, yeah, like the telling my parents and [unintelligible 00:13:45] this to my parents is probably the scariest thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And having to talk to those friends, like right now I don't want to do that. It's- it puts them in a weird place.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Kind of feels like you're climbing Mt. Everest.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you don't have equipment.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It feels like I have to lec- I don't wanna have to lecture them and I don't want it to be like a lecture.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're concerned that they're gonna kind of treat you like a child.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: My parents or my friends?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, oh, you're talking about your friends.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, lecture my-- Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're wondering if they're gonna kind of be like children and you're gonna be like the parent saying-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, and I don't wanna be like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You just wanna be like peers talking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you want them to support you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I wanna stay friends with them. I don't want- I don't want them to just-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You don't wanna lose your support group, yeah. You just wanna them to support you in being healthy, while helping them, raising the babe, and so we're just taking path B. You don't wanna lose them, just maybe the lifestyle it sounds like.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, like if there's a- if there's a balance between maybe not the paths, but the worlds, if there's a balance between that-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm. You kind of wanna have the best of both worlds.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I want the friends and the relationship that I get from my friends, and at the same time, I don't want the party scene that goes with that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, like I-I know I just can't cut off my friends altogether.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, Nina, you know yourself best, and you know, you know, you know what your world looks like and what those, you know, like, you know the support that your friends give you and the support that you get from your family, you know that. Um, and I'm just wondering if maybe we can kind of pick this up, um, in a next visit, but before we go there, I'm just wondering, is there some steps that you would be willing to kind of take or consider, uh, with-with regards to your drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um yeah, like I'm so close anyways, that I know I need to now. Um, and I just also, like, have I completely screwed this up, like, is it already too late?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're concerned about the health of your baby. I just would love to share with you, Nina, that every day without alcohol is a good day for your baby, and you know, starting today to have zero alcohol is a great start, and I'm wondering if that's the sort of something you'd be open to as no more alcohol at this point.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, I have to do.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, sounds like this is really important to you. You want to make this happen.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Is there anything that I can support you with before we wrap up as far as giving up alcohol today?
