utterances.text: I don't think so. I think just knowing that it's not too late already is enough kick in the pants to get started.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You kind of got a reality check today.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: A little bit.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You did really well talking with me today, and I thank you so much for just sharing your heart.

topic: more exercise / increasing activity; weight loss
video_title: Part 1: A Non-Diet Approach with Motivational Interviewing Role Play, Engaging

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, Natalie. I'm Dawn.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hi, Dawn. Nice to meet you.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Nice to meet you, too. Thanks for coming in today.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Thanks for having me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Tell me a little bit about yourself.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So I am, um, 28. And I moved out to Arizona about six months ago. Um, I really enjoy spending time with my family and hanging out with friends whenever I can. Work keeps me pretty busy. Um, But I'm really, um, looking to kind of make some changes to my diet and physical activity. I'm not really happy with where my weight's at right now, and, uh, so I thought it'd be good to come and talk with you about some of that stuff.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, you're feeling a little bit dissatisfied with your health patterns?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Um, I'm really starting to notice how I feel more sluggish and just not-- My mood is shifted a lot too, which at first, I thought was because it's getting colder outside, um, but I do also think it maybe has some relation to my activity, or lack thereof, and also kind of the foods that I'm eating.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so you're feeling some low energy and you know, in the past, when you've been more active and eating differently, you've had more energy?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right. Yeah. Especially during times when I'm more active is when I noticed the biggest cha-change in energy and mood.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Tell me more about that, those previous times that you've been active.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Um, well, I played sports in college, so that kept me pretty busy, and that was really fun, um, and I just think back now to, as much that I would cram into a 24 -hour period, and like, wonder how I did that, but I think that part of it was because I was so active physically, um, I just had way more energy throughout the day, mentally and physically to, um, you know, go to school full-time and-and still socialize with friends and do all that stuff. Um, so when I think back to like, probably like the peak of my life of when I felt my best physically, mentally it was that time.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You had energy, and you were like the Energizer Bunny, just keep going and going and going.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, exactly. And now it's not so much the same. Um, like when I get home from work, I'm pretty exhausted, uh, it takes a lot for me to want to be physically active when I've spent all day staring at a computer and thinking and working. And so, um, yeah, that's probably been my biggest, uh, issue is like when work ends, going home and not really doing anything. Um, just trying to like unwind by watching Netflix or something else, right?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So your days are just as full now that you're working and a career person, um, and your energy level isn't what it used to be. What-- Do you have any ideas about why that might have shifted?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, I think part of it is that when I was in college, it wasn't really an option to go, like, I had to go to practice or I had to do those things because that was, in a sense, my job that was paying for school, um, and now there's not that same commitment to other people or to scholarship money. So that definitely has shifted, um, but I-I do feel like a-an urgency to go it just doesn't seem that like the step that's missing is for me to actually go to a gym or somewhere to be more active. Like, I think I want to it's just the doing it that seems to not happen.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. So in the past, it wasn't up to you whether you had the choice to go be physically active. Now it is up to you, and-and you're looking back at the last few years and saying, I wanna do things differently.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I want to be more physically active than I've been.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I think so. Um, that's not to say like, I wanna go run a marathon but I do think that it would help me a lot in terms of just having a better outlook on life, um, and better energy to- if I were to pick up some type of activity.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great. And you've noticed a mood enhancement effect of exercise.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Tell me more about that. What do you notice specifically about your mood on the days you're physically active?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Just, I'm-I'm just happier and more upbeat and I think that even my outlook is more positive. So like, if I'm sitting in traffic, and I haven't been physically active, I'll probably grumble about it but if I'm sitting in traffic, and I have been, it's like, I just have a different outlook on things and I already feel like I've gotten something accomplished that day. So it just kind of like helps with that ripple effect into my day of like getting more things done.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, you feel more accomplished and-and you feel less irritated by the small stuff.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yeah, exactly.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great. Well, let me see if I've got this all. You came to Arizona six months ago, you're trying to figure out new rhythms and patterns for yourself. You're looking back at the past few years, and in college, you were real active because you were an athlete, and now it's more up to you about making that choice of physical activity, and you're discovering that, um, not being active has affected your energy level and your mood, and that's something you're looking for more of, both of those things, energy and-and a mood booster.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. And then also to, um, like I mentioned, I'm not totally happy with my weight, um, and so hoping too that that would have some impact there and-and maybe help me, um, if my activity kind of gets resolved or improves, then my nutrition also, maybe would go along with it and get better.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Tell me more about your weight concerns. When did you start feeling dissatisfied with your body?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, probably about three, four months ago. Um, yeah, just my clothes started fitting tighter, which wasn't as comfortable, and, um, yeah, just not really super happy with my appearance, which has never really been an issue, um, in my life up until now. I've usually been pretty okay with that, and then in the last three months, I just feel, um, like I've had a lot more of a negative outlook on it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Okay, so it sounds like a sort of a vicious cycle and-and maybe the lacking physical activity has made you feel less confident in yourself. I wonder if that's also a piece of this puzzle since you mentioned that's been a big difference from what was happening in the past.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I think- I think the activity piece and then also to like, the foods that I'm eating, I don't think are that great. So that also kind of does the same thing, I think, to my appearance or the way that I viewed myself.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So you had a pretty strong self-confidence, pretty strong body image all the way up until a few months ago and, um, you're hoping to kind of get back to that place where you feel good about yourself.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great.

video_title: Psychiatric Interviews for Teaching: Somatisation

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Barbara Roberts?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes. Morning.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hello, there.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: My name's Dr. Betty. I'm one of the new GPs in the practice. First of all, what would you like me to call you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, you can call me Barbara. That'll be fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, that's fine. Okay. So, Barbara, I'm seeing you today, um, but I think it's usually Dr. Brown that sees you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Brown is my doctor.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What is it that's brought you to see me today?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I've come about my tummy problem. I've got terrible trouble with my stomach and, uh, Dr. Brown just doesn't seem to be able to get to the bottom of it. And I thought perhaps, uh, I'd come and see you to see if you could help.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Can you tell me a bit more about your tummy problems?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, I-I have this terrible discomfort nearly all the time. Um, it very often feels bloated. I, um, uh, I swing between being constipated and having diarrhea. Um, I have sort of cramping feelings sometimes, and other times it stabs. It's a real stabbing feeling. Um, I often have the urge to go to the toilet and, um, and I pass very smelly wind.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right. So, quite a few symptoms there-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - and some of them sound-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - quite troublesome to you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And how long has this been going on?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I, uh, I've traced it back to a holiday I had in Egypt about four years ago. I had, um, a horrible bout of sickness and diarrhea, and, uh, and I don't think my stomach's ever been really right since then.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Okay. Okay. So you think it began about four years ago after this holiday?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And what's- what sorts of treatments have you tried for-for this before?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, uh, Dr. Brown gave me some muscle relaxants at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, but I've been to the health shop and-and they've been really helpful. They've given me lots of different, um, tablets and medicines-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - for different things. Um, no, oh, and Immodium.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I have Immodium in my handbag all the time, just in case. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. So, these different tablets that you've got from the-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - the herbal shop-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - how are you taking them?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, well, different tablets, you know, I don't have the same problem every day-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - so I'll take some tablets for certain, uh, symptoms, and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - other tablets for other things.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, am I- am I right in thinking you perhaps decide on a day-to-day basis-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - what you're gonna take-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - depending on what your stomach's doing?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. And what about tests? Have you had any tests for these problems?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes, uh, I had, uh, in the early days, I had a gastros-gas-- What are they called?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: A gastroscopy.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That's it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You got the tube down-down from the top?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, and at the same time I had a barium enema.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That was very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, but, um, no, I've tried-- Well, you-- I don't think he's tried enough tests because he said after that, that they didn't find anything-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and he-he's-he's just not sent me for anymore. That's it now-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - as far as he's concerned. Sent me back to the doctor.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. It sounds as though you're-you're not happy with that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, you know, I think that actually, the NHS are running out of money, aren't they? And he's-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - decided that I've had enough tests.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, um, you know, if you go on the Internet-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - there's loads of tests that he could have sent me for.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, if I had a bit more money, I'd go private.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just don't think he's got to the bottom of it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. So you feel as though actually, enough hasn't been done in the way of-of tests?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, he's not. There's loads more he could do. I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Okay. It sounds like you-you've had these problems now for about four years.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You've-you've got a lot of various symptoms in your stomach.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, you've tried a lot of tablets. Some prescribed, some herbal remedies-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - and you've had some investigations, but you're not entirely happy that-that you haven't been investigated thoroughly enough.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Is that- is that about-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'd say so, yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - if I got the story right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And can I ask you, Barbara, how-how is all of this affecting you day-to-day? How's-how's it affecting your life?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, well, it's had quite-quite a big impact. Um, I mean, the first thing, the biggest thing, I suppose, is that I-I went from being full-time to part-time at work.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just couldn't sit all day comfortably.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, and so I went part-time, but in the end, I, uh, about a year ago, I stopped work altogether.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I miss that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I miss the girls. We used to, uh, we used to go out at least once a week.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: To the pictures or for a drink. That's one thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sounds as though that's something you quite enjoyed.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, so I-- Yes. Yes, we used to have a laugh.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I used to go to Swing and Shape. I used to go to an exercise class-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - that was, um, I miss the exercise, actually. That was, um, once a week, but you know, the thing was I wasn't comfortable, never felt quite right doing all this exercise. I was always worried I was gonna be taken short or-- So I stopped that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, then-- Well, my husband and I used to go out for meals.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That's another thing we don't do anymore now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, mm. Yeah, it's quite a few things, really.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, it does- it does sound as though over the last few years your life has really changed-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - quite a lot because of these symptoms.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It sounds- it sounds like you're doing the review of the things that you used to do.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, what is it you'd spend your average day doing now?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I potter around the house-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - um, I spend perhaps a little bit too much time watching. I've got a bit hooked on daytime television, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, they draw you in, don't they?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: They certainly do.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I read a bit-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - the old magazines, but, uh, generally, I'm at home.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. And have there been any times over the last four years that you've noticed any significant changes in your symptoms? For example, have there been any times when things have been better for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, last year, um, my son got married-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - and I-I have to say I was worried that, um, that I wouldn't be able to cope with it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That I-I wouldn't be feeling well enough, but surprisingly enough, um, I was in good form, and I think it was about three weeks in the summer, getting ready for it-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - and the whole hoo-ha of the wedding.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But I was in good- in really good form for that. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That was a good time.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. And how were you tummy symptoms then?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I hardly noticed them.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, it, uh, it seemed to, uh, clear up.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Which was good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. That's interesting.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And are there any times when your-your tummy symptoms bother you more? Seem particularly bad?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, it's- I'm-I'm having a bit of a bad patch at the moment.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's particularly, um, uncomfortable. Um, I have to say I do notice it when my husband's away. He-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - he travels with his job, and he-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - can be away a couple of times a month.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, and that's not-- It-it's very often not good then, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. So you notice it's a bit worse when your husband's not around? Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm. Maybe I'm thinking about it a bit more, I don't know, when he's not there.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. I know you've been seeing Dr. Brown about this for the last few years.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What is it that he's said that he thinks might be wrong with you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, he's-he thinks it's all in my head.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know, he's- he says it's stress.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And what do you think?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I mean, it can't all be in my head. I get too much physical pain-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - for it to be in my head. I mean, it's real. It's-it's real pain.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And have you had any thoughts yourself about what you think might be causing it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I-I did think that perhaps it was an infection that hadn't cleared up-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - in the early stages, but, um, I think, um, I-I mean, sometimes I think it's IBS. A friend of mines has got that and it sounds similar, and then-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - other times I'll think, "I wonder if it's an ulcer."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, on a really bad day, I start to think it might be cancer.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, my mother-in-law- my mother-in-law died of cancer last year and she had a, um, a growth that-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - the-the doctor didn't investigate.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But by the time they'd found it, it was the size of a football-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, dear.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - and it was- it was too late to operate then.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, you know, when I go to bed at night now, um, I just feel to make sure there's nothing different going on.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, uh, yeah, I worry about that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you're- you-you're kind of prodding, having a feel at night?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: To see if you can feel anything?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just want to make sure there's nothing changing down there, you know?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So just to-to make sure that I've got the-the story straight, you've-you've seen Dr. Brown for a couple of years.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You've-you've tried a variety of medications-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - some prescribed, some-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - from the-the herbal shop. None of them really made a great deal of difference. You've had some investigations-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - but you perhaps feel you've not had enough investigations. And at times, you worry that this could be something quite serious like a-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - a cancer. Is that-- Have I got the-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - story right?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'd say so.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Barbara, what was it that you were hoping that I'd do for you today?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I thought, you know, you're a new doctor here-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - and you've just finished your medical training. I wondered whether, you know, with new eyes and a new way of looking at-at the problem-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - um, you-you probably know about different tests, new tests, that my doctor doesn't know about, you know, new developments.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So perhaps you could send me for some different tests.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Right. So you were hoping that I'd send you for more tests?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I think there's-there's got to be something that a test might-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - might reveal.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Well, I think, Barbara, having-having heard your story, and heard about the symptoms, I'm not sure that actually sending you for more tests at this point would be the most useful thing that we could do for you. And the reason for that is because you've-you've had some of the main investigations in the last couple of years, and-and they've not shown anything. And your symptoms haven't really changed that much. So it's very unlikely that if we were to send you for more tests now that-that they'd show anything different than what we already know. So a bit-- I think it would be a waste of time for you to go for more tests.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So-so like, do you think it's all in my head then? You're gonna be like Dr. Brown. You think I'm imagining all of this?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh, no. I think that you clearly have pain, and clearly you have lots of physical symptoms, and they're clearly getting in the way of-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -your life and causing you a lot-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -of disability.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I guess- I guess the way I think about these things is that they're not necessarily either all in the mind or all in the body.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sometimes these things can go together. Uh, I guess I'm thinking about how you told me that last year, when your son got married, uh, and you were very busy-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - and quite happy, that somehow your symptoms seemed less.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And, uh, when your husband's away, which is something you don't like very much, sometimes, somehow, your symptoms then will seem greater. So, I guess what I'm wondering, Barbara, is if there might be some kind of a link with you between how you're feeling in your mind, and what's going on in your life, and-and how much your symptoms trouble you. Do you think that's a possibility?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I can't see that my mind can be causing this amount of pain.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm. I'm not saying that the pain's in your mind. Um, I guess what I'm saying is that sometimes the way that we feel, and the way that our lives are going, can impact how we notice our symptoms. Given that we've tried medication for you, and we've tried investigations, and we've drawn a blank really, with those, none of those have really helped you-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - I guess I'm wondering whether now it would be a good idea to try a different approach to your problems.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: What-what sort of approach?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, I guess, thinking a little bit about those other areas of your life, um, uh, I'm thinking about the fact that over the last four years, your life's really changed. It seems to have really shrunk down.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it sounds as though you're not doing lots of the things that you used to do. That you-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - used to get pleasure out of. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I just can't do them.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I can't- I can't do them anymore.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And I guess I wonder-- Uh, it sounds as though you've-you've dropped doing those things because you felt you couldn't do them, but I wonder if, in a funny way, what's happened is the fact that you're not doing those pleasurable things now, has kind of fed into you feeling-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - unhappy with the way that-that your life is at the moment. And-and I guess I wonder whether that can then make your symptoms worse for you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, I guess what I'd be wondering is whether one of the approaches we need to be using now is thinking about what you do with your life, and what you do with your day, and maybe trying to bring back some of those pleasurable things, you know, even if it's just meeting up-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - with your-your female friends once a week, and whether actually doing those sorts of things might generally-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - improve your quality of life. I'm also thinking about the tablets that you're taking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And the fact that you-you seem to be taking quite a lot of them, and I'm wondering whether it's worth, though, sitting and looking at them and-and maybe trying to rationalize them a little bit, and really decide which are helping you, which are doing nothing, and which may actually be making some of your symptoms worse, I guess.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What would you think about trying that slightly different approach for say-say two or three months, just to see whether or not it makes any difference?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, two or three months is a long time if there is something going on. I mean, that's what happened to my mother-in-law, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: They-they left her and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - didn't spot it and—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, I guess if we- if we did decide to-to work together like this-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - in this new approach, I'd be seeing you regularly. We can keep an eye on your symptoms, and if they change, then we can investigate as appropriate. But if they stay the same, then, you know, we can be-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - pretty clear that there's nothing new happening that-that we're missing.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How would that sound?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, uh, what are you saying then? That I should come back and see you?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I think that would be a good idea. I think we've only just begun to talk about it-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - and I think perhaps you need to have a bit of time to think about it and then perhaps come back. Perhaps if you're booked in for a double slot next week, and that would give us a good chunk of time to think about this new approach.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And perhaps if you could also bring your-your tablets in or-or make a list of them, we can look at what you're taking and perhaps go from there. How would that sound, Barbara?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay. Well, uh, to make an appointment for next week.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And come and see you again-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - and talk about it a bit more?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yes. I think so.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I think that would be a good- a good start.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: All right. And I'll make a list of the tablets that I'm taking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I won't bring all the bottles down.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, shall I see you again next week?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'll make an appointment for next week. Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you, Barbara.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Bye-bye.

video_title: Part Two: Motivational Interviewing in an Integrated Care Setting (Counselor Scenario)

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, Sarah, it's great to meet you. My name is Delwyn, and I'm a counselor here at the clinic. And I heard from your nurse practitioner that you recently had an annual exam in which the topics of smoking and alcohol use came up. Would you mind filling me in a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, um, last week I met with my nurse practitioner, and I ge-I guess she's worried with how much I'm smoking and drinking right now. I mean, I-I did agree I would work on the smoking and try to cut back on that. But, as far as the drinking, I-I don't really think I drink that much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you've decided you wanna cut back on your smoking a little bit, but, you're not really concerned about your drinking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right, I mean, I don't drink that much and, honestly, it-it's just a good way to relax.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It's a nice sort of form of stress relief.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, exactly. You know, it's kind of like that me time at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sort of escape from your hectic schedule.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. You know, I have a two-year-old son, and then, I work full-time. And, I also started going back to school. So, you know, just trying to juggle all that stuff. You know, it's tiring, and so, you know, at the end of the day, I just- I wanna relax and enjoy myself.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you're working, and then, on top of that, juggling being a single mom and going to school?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, and for work, you know, I'm a server. So, I'm on my feet all day, you know, and it's-it's really tiring.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It's pretty exhausting work.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, you know, it's hard trying to please customers all day. And then, at the same time, I'm-I'm worrying, am I making enough money to support my son, you know?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you're not only doing really tiring work and going to school, but you're also worrying about your finances.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, and then, you know, with going back to school, you know, I have to figure out how I'm going to pay for everything. So, you know, i-it's just a lot right now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, it does. It sounds like a lot that you're trying to deal with, and it makes sense that you feel like you need some kind of break or reward.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, tell me a little bit more about your drinking. Tell me a little bit about how much you're drinking, and, um, the pattern, and what raised concern.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, that's the thing. I-I don't really understand what raised concern. I mean, I don't drink that much, you know. I've-I've gone up to maybe two drinks a day max, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you're drinking, perhaps, two drinks a day. Um, and I'm wondering, what have you heard about the recommendations for drinking levels?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, will you be interested in hearing about those recommendations?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, so, the recommendation for women is to have no more than three drinks a day, and no more than seven drinks over the course of a week. Yeah, um, and, really, the reason for those recommendations is to just reduce the risk that people have trouble with accidents, or chronic diseases. Like certain types of cancers, or high blood pressure, and then also psychological problems. I don't know what you think about all that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know, i-it just surprises me because, I mean, two drinks a day, that-that doesn't seem like a problem or risky, you know. And, I have family members who drink a lot more than that per day, and, it's not a problem for them. So, i-it just surprises me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It just doesn't seem that abnormal to you, especially when you compare it with your family.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. And then, I don't know, I-I'm just getting kind of annoyed, honestly, because, you know, I did agree I would try to work on my smoking, you know. But, with this whole drinking thing, it's like everything that I enjoy, you know, is being taken away from me right now. And so, if I give up drinking, like, what am I going to have to enjoy myself, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, you really feel like you need that reward.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And then it also sounds like, um, your drinking has perhaps increased a little bit over time?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, I guess it has. Probably just with being so stressed out every day, you know. I mean, I'm in my second semester of school right now, and so, adding that to everything, uh, it's a lot. And, you know, I'm trying to figure out child carry. Um, normally, my mom will watch my son, but, lately, she can't always. And so, I'm always kind of worrying like, will she be able to, you know. So, i-it's just stressful.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, and so it sounds like you've noticed that the more stressed you're feeling, the more you're drinking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I-I guess that's right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, let me summarize a little bit what you've told me. It sounds like you have a pretty hectic, stressful life, and you really feel like you need some kind of-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -reward or stress relief. Um, and then, on the other hand, you've noticed, um, that your drinking has increased a little bit over time. And also that the more stressed you're fe- you feel, the more you're inclined to drink.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, I'm wondering, have you noticed any problems from your drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. I guess, you know, the one- the one thing I can think of is, I mean, there will be evenings when I just kind of want to get my son to bed a little earlier, just so that I can have that alone time to unwind, you know, maybe-maybe smoke, have a couple drinks. Um, but, I do feel guilty about that sometimes, because, I should enjoy spending time with my son, but, instead, you know, I'm just wanting to be by myself and relax, you know. So—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you've noticed that it's starting to call to you a little bit in the evenings.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it's perhaps taking you away from things that are more important to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it doesn't feel good?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And so, it sounds like there's a bit of a dilemma there, because-- And I guess we should be clear, it's not the occasional drink that's an issue. Um, it's-it's really the quantity of drinking, and-and whether your drinking is escalating and interfering with things that are, perhaps, more important.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you've perhaps never seen it in that light before.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. And, i-it's just, it's really hard to take in right now. I mean, yeah. I-I've never thought about it like this. And, so, you know, I-I do feel kind of worried.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I-it seems like it-it would be quite a hard pattern to change.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, i-it's part of my routine right now, and, you know, I-I don't want to sacrifice something I enjoy, but, you know, I'm trying really hard, you know, to be a good mom. I'm-I'm trying to, you know, go-go back to school. I'm trying to work. So, I don't know how I can do all of that if I don't have a way to enjoy myself or relax, you know?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, it seems like it would be really difficult to change because it's something that's really important to you right now.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: But on the other hand, it does sound like there are things that you- that you value that you don't want the drinking to interfere with.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, I guess I'm wondering if you've given any thought to other ways in which you could cope with stress without relying on the drinking so much.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, you know, if there was some way that I could relieve some of my stress, I think I would feel better, and, you know, maybe at night, I wouldn't feel like I had to unwind in the same way.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, if you could somehow tackle some of these stressful issues, um, that could make a difference, and, what-what would that be, for example?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, you know, probably my biggest problem is just childcare. You know, my mom normally watches my son, but she's been kind of backing out lately. utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, having more reliable childcare could make a big difference.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it sounds like your mom has been an option in the past, but perhaps not so much anymore.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, she watches him so much. I think she's just probably getting stressed out too. And, I feel bad because, you know, it's not her son, so i-it shouldn't be her problem, but, I need something that I can rely on better.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, one thing that could make a big difference is if you could figure out some sort of more reliable, affordable childcare, and that would help you not want to drink as much.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I mean, most of my problems always go back to money. You know, i-if I had more money, I could afford daycare, I could work less hours, you know? So, yeah. It's-it's normally related to money.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. It-it sounds like, um, you know, money could make a big difference, and you are working full time and trying to go to school to address that in the long run. Um, but on the other hand, you know, it sounds like you have some other ideas of cope- of how you might cope with stress better. Um, so, I guess I'm-I'm wondering, given our conversation so far, kind of where you are with everything.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, we started off talking about how your drinking has sort of drifted into a risky area, and it would be advisable to cut back. Um, but it sounds like you feel like that's fairly important to you and not something you necessarily want to do. But on the other hand, we've talked about ways in which that perhaps could be made a bit easier, but I'm not sure if you're ready to tackle that or pursue that right now. I'm just kind of wondering where you are.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I'm ready to consider changing my drinking, but, as far as actually doing it, I-I don't know. I mean, I have a lot of problems that I'm trying to work out right now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, um, it would perhaps be helpful if you could narrow it down to just one thing, and what would that be?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Childcare, probably.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah. It sounds like from everything you're saying, that keeps coming up as one of the main issues. Um, so there may be some resources I can point you towards, but I'm- guess I'm wondering, have you looked into alternatives, more affordable, reliable childcare?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not really. I mean, I just normally see if my mom can watch my son, so, you know, I haven't really looked around.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, one thing you could consider is talking to one of our social workers, they sort of specialize in helping people who have a lot on their plate identifying resources that they may need, uh, things you haven't thought of or aren't aware of. utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Great. Well, I can definitely set you up with that, and you can-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -um, try to tackle, um, your childcare issue, um, with some assistance. Is there anything else you'd like to do, um, for example, would you be interested in talking with me again, um, just as things progress?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I-I think I would. I mean, it's-it's been nice to just talk about everything that's going on.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So, these are not problems that are going to go away in a week. It's going to take some time to resolve. Okay, great. So, um, it sounds like we have a couple of things, uh, to pursue.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Anything-anything else?

utterances.speaker: client

video_title: Rowing with Confidence

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Tanya, for meeting with me today and talking about this. utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, you know, I have a lot of anxiety, and so there's this test that I have to take. It's a big test and I've kind of been putting it off just 'cause I get very anxious. utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. This anxiety is this obstacle for you and it sounds like it, then you're just not feeling confident that you could do it and do it successfully to this exam.

utterances.text: So that's really encouraging you thinking about how good you'll feel afterwards once it's done and taken.

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: Yeah. You kind of want to avoid that. Yeah. Have those other feelings that could come up and if you don't have.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I'd love to hear from you. When was the time in the past that you were feeling anxious about something and you actually did it and it turned out well?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, I would say maybe like four or five years ago, um, I had to do a recording for work and I did not want to do it. utterances.text: Um, it made me feel good.

utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So for you to create opportunities to create those moments that you can have that feeling again

utterances.text: Right

utterances.text: And you just mentioned too, you feel really proud of yourself.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And maybe just having that faith in myself that, you know, that I can do it instead of just thinking that I can't.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So that positive self-talk could really go a long way for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So to summarize, it sounds like you are still feeling kind of anxious about this test coming up, you've rescheduled it, um, over the past couple years. Yet, this time around, you seem more confident to just get it done. And you've even mentioned times in the past where you were feeling anxious and you were successful about it and that you felt proud about yourself. And you liked the way it means, you see yourself and how others saw you, and it seems like y-you're ready to finish this exam and-and remind yourself that you can be successful?

utterances.speaker: client

video_title: Adolescent brief intervention: "Jacob"

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, Jacob, everything looks very normal on your physical exam. Do you have any questions for me?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. I see that you filled out our, um, alcohol and drug questionnaire. Is it okay if we go through this together?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What we talk about is confidential. I only tell your parents about what we say if you give your permission or if I become worried about a danger to-to you or to someone else. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, let's take a look. So I see that you have marked that you sometimes use alcohol, and that you have used alcohol to relax, feel better about yourself or fit in. Do you mind telling me a little bit more about your alcohol use?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's not a big deal. Sometimes with my friends, we'll drink a few beers and when we're hanging out or when we're at a party, and sometimes rum and cokes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so how many do you usually have at a time?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, three or four, probably. I don't keep track.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And how often?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, probably about once or twice a month.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, you drink with friends, sort of three or four beers or mixed drinks, one or two times a month. How long have you been doing that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Probably since last October.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, for about six months. I'm curious. What do you like about drinking alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: What do I like about it?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I don't know. It's just fun to drink with my friends, like when we're at a party at someone else's house, and we're drinking with other people that we don't know. It tastes good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, it sounds like you feel relaxed and have fun when you're drinking with friends and you like the taste.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. I'm also curious, are there any parts about your alcohol use that you don't like?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I don't like when I get sick in the mornings 'cause of hangovers and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -when I start throwing up, that's not- I don't like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Have you ever experienced a-a blackout, like when you've been drinking and you wake up and you don't remember what happened?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, but that happened to someone I know, though.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And have you had any problems related to-to your drinking alcohol, like at home or school or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, one time I missed first period of school 'cause I had a hangover and I was late getting up.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm, mom got mad at me 'cause I wouldn't get out of bed and she said she knew I had a hangover.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Have you told your mother that you drink with your friends?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, but I got grounded for two weeks after that. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So more negative things about your drinking, like getting into trouble with your mom and missing a class at school when you had a hangover?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, but I only missed school once.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. I see on the questionnaire that you have not ridden in a car with someone who's been drinking and you haven't driven a car, um, after you've been drinking. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's great. And I hope you continue to avoid those things. As your doctor, I want you to know that I'm concerned about your drinking. When teens drink, things can go wrong, like injuring yourself. Even when you don't drink too excess, though, your brain is still developing and is very sensitive to the effects of alcohol.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's why I recommend that all my adolescent patients not drink at all. So if you were thinking today about how ready you feel to stop drinking alcohol on a scale of zero to ten, with zero not being ready at all and ten feeling very ready, what number would you pick?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, probably a five.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: A five? So, I'm curious. Why didn't you pick a lower number like a two or three that would mean you're only a little bit ready to stop drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I guess I'm just tired of getting in trouble.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What could you do to avoid getting into trouble?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, not drink.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: [chuckles] Have you ever tried not drinking or stopping drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What some people your age do is try stopping drinking for a period of time just to see what that feels like.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I could probably do that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, how long do you think you could go without drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Do you think you could go two months without drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, probably.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What things would make it easier for you to not drink?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I could probably drink something else when my friends are drinking, like just coke.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Anything else to make things easier for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I can probably hang out with some of my friends who don't drink or inviting them to parties and having fun 'cause not everyone drinks at parties.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Is there anybody in your life that you can talk to about this, who give you some support for not drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. The-- My friends who don't drink would probably be happy that I'm not drinking either and yes, they'd support me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great. So you've come up with some reasons to stop drinking, like having hangovers and throwing up and getting into trouble. And you've developed some strategies to-to try to not drink, like spending more time with friends who don't drink or having non-alcoholic drinks when people around you are drinking alcohol. I think that's a great plan. I'm really proud of you for giving this a try. How about if I have you make an appointment for two months from now and then I'll see you back and we can see how things are going?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.
