utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right, Catherine, welcome back. I'll be interested to, sort of, after we met last time, what-what were you-- what have you been thinking about over the week 'cause, you know, I-I remembered last time I asked you what you were thinking about coming, but-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -what was different this time and your thoughts about coming?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I suppose, my expectations are a wee bit clearer as to why I'm here.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I guess, I'm-- It made me think about how much money I have been losing recently. So, yeah. I'm happier to be here. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, okay. So, there's a shift from last time?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. My sense is we'll be able to work pretty well together. That's my, sort of, sense of, uh-- After last time, I thought, you know, "Here's a young woman who's, you know, got some energy to get things together-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and, uh--" So, really, what we'd like to talk about today is-is get a sense of, um-- Let's talk about the things that would be good to work with, um, over the next, you know, nine months together, really.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, one of the things that we started to touch on, last time, was this issue of gambling, and, um, you were talking, last time, about how the gambling had, sort of, got you into trouble with your family.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So, thinking about, like, you know, last time, you-you started to say that, well, you thought it was-- you deserved it and there was some thinking around that, so I'm, sort of, wondering how open you are to-to exploring that from some different angles?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm happy to explore it, so to speak. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, so how-how-- You know, like-- 'Cause, sometimes, when we start to open things up, and then you think, "Oh, it feels a bit uncomfortable." So, how do you manage things when you get uncomfortable? How have you managed those in the past?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm. I don't know, I probably lock off a wee bit. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. So, how would I know if we were talking and you were blocking off? What would I notice, uh, in our session together?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, um. I'm sure you've already noticed. [chuckles] Um, I don't know, probably fidget.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That's why I am still a bit—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So-so, what would be really helpful maybe because I might miss it, you know, so, like, could you tell me? It would be really helpful if—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: When I'm feeling uncomfortable?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. If you could just say, "Ken, hi, I am starting to, you know, tune it out here, starting to get uncomfortable," that would be really helpful.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, thanks for that, okay. So, let's think about the-- It has to do with how you just sorted out the thing around the gambling 'cause last time you were here, you told me that you get a buzz, you know, it seemed like you were gambling a bit more than your girlfriends were aware of, and-and you said you owe one of your friends some money.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, um, how serious do you think this issue is to sort?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: [sighs] I suppose it's really serious if I wanna get out of my-my-my debt.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Credit comes out of my ears, and mom and dad aren't bailing me out anymore, so-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -I suppose, I've gotta sort it out myself.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, again, on a scale of 1 to 100, how serious-- how important is it to sort it out? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: About 80. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: About 80? Right up there, yeah, yeah? And another question that's, sort of, related to that, how confident are you that you can, you know, you can actually get it sorted and get on with life?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'm gonna say, I'm completely confident.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah? But, what would-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -your level be on a scale of 1 to 100? Where does your confidence sit?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: What, on my confidence to stop? [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, to get it sorted. Not necessarily to stop. But we don't- we don't know whether-whether stopping's the right answer here, I don't know, but-but, your confidence to sort it out.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's hard when it's part of your lifestyle, you know?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: When I went with my girlfriends to the pub last night and I went and hit a bit of a flutter-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -so, you know, I think I'm a bit weird if I just sit-sit at the bar on my own. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah, so-so, you fluttered last night with them?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yep. Okay, okay. And-and when they stopped fluttering, were you still fluttering or did you stop with them? Where-where were you with—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, I had to stop halfway 'cause I'd ran out of money. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Okay. Yeah, yeah. So, you were saying before that, you know, there was, you know, money you couldn't really afford-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -'cause you owed your mom and dad some money, and they weren't bailing you out anymore, and you had to go out and find some money, I think?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah? Yeah. Yep. So, it seems like almost, like, you're still in the behavior, you know, still creating some problems?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: There's some feelings when you, kind of, think about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know, but I'd like to get back on track, but—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not really planning on spending my life in debt. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't mind traveling, and, you know, I've got friends that are saving for the [unintelligible 00:18:27] and I'm 25 and working in retail, and got four credit cards-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -so I won't be doing any traveling any time soon.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, again, that, sort of, sounds really important. So, what's-what's your dreams? What are your dreams? Where do you wanna be in five years' time? Where does Catherine wanna be? What do you wanna be doing? What are your dreams?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe I wanna have traveled and found the man of my dreams. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know. Kids maybe, but-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -I'm not gonna- [sighs] I'm not gonna make a decent mom the way I am, at the moment, am I? So I probably need to get on track at some stage. [chuckles] I'll be pushing 30 and still in debt, at this rate.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, okay. So, it seems like you're-you're, kind of, in a state in your life of considering your next steps.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah? Yeah. "Do I continue with the, you know, my little current lifestyle," and you are so much the party girl you used to be-- I was speaking to last time-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -wasn't that-- Is that right? Yeah? So, "Do I live a party lifestyle-- party-girl kind of lifestyle, or am I got some other dreams to follow?" So, they're hard calls to make. And-and it all-- And there are no three ways. We will have to make those calls at some point.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And, my sense, is that some of the challenge for you, at the moment? Yeah?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: When you think five years ahead, which-which position do you wanna be in? Which-which feels best? Party girl still, you know, with those four credit cards maxed out major, or would you wanna be actually, you know, thinking about having traveled and, you know, maybe, starting a family, those other things? Which-which direction feels best for you at this point?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Party girl at 30s is a bit sad, really, isn't it? [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know. It's been fun up to now-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What's your hunch? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -but I really do wanna travel, so.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. Where in particular? You've got any ideas about what—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, Egypt, always been, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Egypt?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh, what's that about Egypt, that, uh?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, I just think it's just fascinating.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Just the, um, the outlook, and the culture and the history and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -somewhere I've always wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's not the safest place at the moment, mind you, but [chuckles].

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: No, that's true.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: But for obvious times.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It could be very different.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay, so you've been-- How long have you had this-this idea for that that's what you'd like and that's where you'd like to go?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, since I was young, early teens.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, yeah?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm. So how much does the kind of, uh, current lifestyle rob you of that, you know, take away from that dream?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, well, I suppose with the amount of money I've spent over the last five years I probably could have gone to Egypt and back five times by now. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: There you go. So there's some decisions to make around, uh, which dream, which path you wanna follow.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm. What do you reckon to be the-the hardest bit of taking that pathway to-to traveling and realizing the-the dream? What would be the tough things that you'd have to confront?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I believe then to cut off some of my friendships. Um, 'cause since you see that's, you know, part of their lifestyle.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. It will be a big change.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, mm-hmm. So I see this is- this is something you've been thinking about for a while. So how far away do you think you are from that change? You know, 'cause obviously it can-can be on the never, never, but how far away are you from it, making some decisions about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Seems like a bit of an unrealistic dream. Um, and I'd like to take the first step but, uh, that's gonna be easy.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: No, no. That'll be easy. So what is the first step for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Probably, um, [chuckles] cutting up the credit cards for a starter, and trying to restrain myself, and not to be led into temptation, I suppose, so.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know, if the pokies are at the pubs, just don't go to the pub. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, it's hard, isn't it? It's hard being in the pub thing, in that environment.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: We'd-we'd-we'd have an illustration for them, I suppose. We call those high-risk situations. You know, it's that-- so you might learn some language about some sort of the way that we describe-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -it and stuff, but, you know, being at the pub, you know, you want to sort of get the buzz of, you know, gambling, you know, horror situation, really easy to just go against what you decide that you wanted to do. Yeah?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah? So how today have you sort of found some ways to manage that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I haven't managed it to-to this point, so [chuckles] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I suppose I've just got to get tougher with myself.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. I think somewhat being tough with yourself, what-- yeah, people often say that, but, you know, it's not-- I think there are some things that you can do, and you've already-already identified a really good strategy.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: What? Cutting off some of my friendships?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, it's a couple of ideas. O-one, thinking about who your friends are and will your friends support you to realize your dream of traveling to Egypt.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, and the other idea you talked about before was, actually, cutting up your credit cards. So kind of amazing what that thing makes there on different cards isn't it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It's very helpful and healthy. So, yeah, a couple of really good ideas already you've got, guess so?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So that's-that's some work that we can continue to work with. Yeah? Yeah?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So 'cause-'cause I asked the question before, is what might be the hardest thing, and you'd identified that your friends, you know, could be one of the habits.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yep, yep. Could that mean that some of your friends are probably moving around some similar sort of stuff like you, wondering about where they're going and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -what they want to further their dreams, yeah?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so we talked about sort of where things you-w-- Where you might be in five years and which path you wanna take, yep, yep? And you seemed very clear about it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. Something we can- we can do over the next while is-is really get some very concrete things in place to support you to do that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So what's one thing you can do between now and the next time we meet?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Find the scissors. [laughs]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, find the scissors.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Cut out the girls.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Then, um, I don't know if the debts are still gonna be there or not but I-I've gotta find-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -a way to pay them off and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Truly.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -I don't know how I'm gonna do that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay, so sounds like so-some budget to buy stuff will be helpful.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, and of the things that-that we often put people in touch with here is some budget advice service, it's a great service here, um, and something that you can get to.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So let's talk about how we can organize a-a meeting with them.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, that will be good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

video_title: How to Do Motivational Interviewing (MI) Role Play - 2

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, uh, I guess the issue is that, um, you know, my doctor seems to think that my-my blood pressure's a little high, but I really don't think that there's a problem. And you know, I eat really well. Um. And, you know, she suggested that, um, I watch my caffeine but really, caffeine is not a problem for me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Um, but we were talking a little bit earlier-- earlier in our conversation, you had said that you did feel like it was maybe causing some of your agitation. So it's a little bit of, I'm not sure of what-- Um, so where are we? Did-did you-- do you feel like you do have some agitation out of coffee, or is it just no problem at all?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, you know, sometimes it makes me a little jittery and, you know, I have to go to the bathroom more frequently than some of my co-workers, but-- And-and working, um, in the hospital, they don't really look so highly on-on going the bathroom frequently. But you know, it-it keeps me awake, it keeps me aware, it-it makes me more able to like, you know, do my job better. And so I really don't see that it's a-it's a real issue.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, you know, and-and-- I mean, maybe my blood pressure is a little high, but—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So let me see if I had this. So y- so you got some positives, the-the awareness, and then you feel kinda on your game?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, and then there's some negatives with, um, you know, your-your co-workers, um, that they don't, you know-- then your boss may not want you, you know, checking out-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -on the hospital floor, you know, for frequently.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Gotta stay on, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, and then the blood pressure thing. Does that sound about right?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. Well, you know, and sometimes, like I said, it does kind of make me a little jittery and, um, I don't know. I-I-I'm not- I'm not as happy and relaxed as I normally am. But you know, I-I really like it, and-and like I said, it makes me more aware of what's going on and-and I'm-- I-I feel like I'm much more observant.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. How about frequency? Do you feel like you're good on how much coffee you're drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I have about four cups a day.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. And that feels about right to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I've-- I mean, it's the co-workers that-that work at night. Gosh, they bring in a carafe.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, uh, I-I can only imagine-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -what-what their bodies are like.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. What would happen if you-- if you looked at, maybe reducing that with that habit? Would that get rid of maybe some of the things that are problematic?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Reducing it, like-- what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: The number. Just the number.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah but, I mean, how-how much are we talking?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I don't-- you tell me. I mean, um, you're-you're drinking four a day.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You're probably-- you know, because I-I gotta have that morning cup, I really-- you know I really like waking up and-and that whole ritual. The, um-- you know, making the coffee and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -I just really like the flavors.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So I-I definitely don't want to give that up, but—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I gotcha. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So that one's important.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And then, of course, you know, working a 12-hour shift, I-I really think that, you know, the afternoon to keep me going until the evening is-is a really good idea too.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I could probably get up the mid-morning.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I think that's great.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I think so. So you've identified one of the four that might-- you might be willing to-to try-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -for a while to-to let go of. What do you- what do you think of that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think that does sound all right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think I could do that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Tell me what you know about the flu shot?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, well, I know the flu can be pretty bad, but I'm in pretty good health, so I don't really feel like I need it. Uh, it's kind of just more for old people, right?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm, um, so you're thinking it's really just for people who are-are vulnerable to illness?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Would it be okay if I shared a little more information with you about the flu vaccine and the importance of it?

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: Yeah. I just sort of did a bit of search on the internet and stuff and just read about this place, so I just thought I'll—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. So it sounds like you thought there was something that, uh, that you needed to look at, something that was concerning you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I guess. I-I suppose I hadn't really thought about it till they sat me down, and you know- I mean I could, uh, I could understand a little bit of where they were coming from, so yeah, I thought I'd—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: They were concerned for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah, which kind of was a bit of a sh-shock, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You were surprised?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah, 'cause, you know, I don't know. You know, you see on movies when people sort of intervene or say, "You know, you need to go and get help." And then-- I don't know. Like you know those characters and, they-they do need help, you know-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -because they're fucked.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And you kind of go, "Woah. That's not me." So it's about am I—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're not sure that applies to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, or well, not to that extent, you know what I mean? Like, I-I would-- l didn't think I was at anywhere near a point that I would need to be sat down and intervened with-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -if you know what I mean.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I suppose.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand you so far, something's concerning you and something's concerning your friends-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -but you're not sure whether it's- whether-- just how bad it is or- and you're just wanting to check that out?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, 'cause, I mean, you know, they are my friends and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - you know, I'm not gonna be so narrow-minded as to say for sure that, you know, they're entirely wrong 'cause there's a big group of them, you know? And they do care, so obviously, there's something there that I might have overlooked. But on the other hand, I'm sort of like, "Well, was it that bad?" And you know, "Was that- was that really necessary?" But I, you know, I thought I'd give them the benefit of the doubt and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and just check it up, yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Because they care about you and-and you respect what they say, and you're wondering whether something about what they're saying may be right, but let's check that out a bit?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, pretty right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, let's do some checking out.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay, cool.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So tell me a little bit about what you're doing, what is- what is the concern that they are raising.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, dr-drugs, I guess.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm, yeah. Sort of kind of do a bit of P now and again-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and, um, I guess less often, I do a bit of, you know, I smoke a little bit and, um, party pills in the- in the weekend sometimes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Tell me a little bit about what now and again means, and-and-and how often.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, a couple of times a week maybe.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Is this- is this with, uh, with the drug?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: This is meth you're talking about? A couple of times a week?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, yeah. Yeah. So I guess when I put it that way, it does sound quite a lot, but it doesn't feel a lot, you know? If you know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, maybe, we c-- we can check that out to see whether-whether it's a lot or-- But maybe also importantly to-to discuss with you what the effects are and-and-and what your concerns are about it. But help me to understand a little bit more of what it's like for you. Tell me- tell me what are the things about your, uh, use of meth that you- that you've liked that you found good for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right. Um, I suppose it's kind of hand-in-hand with just hanging out with, sort of, some new scene that I've-- Like, um, I moved to Auckland maybe three years ago.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, um, I still live in Palmy and, so as you can imagine, it's sort of a bit different down there. And, um, kind of just when I first got here I was sorta introduced a little bit to, um, like do you know Family Bar on-on [unintelligible 00:06:49]?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I know Family Bar, yes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. It's that sort of- that sorta scene, that kind of, um, gay scene, I guess. And, like, it's not something I'd really thought about before and-- But then kinda hung out there and just met these people that were sort of like you don't really get there much Palmy. Well, I mean I suppose you do, but they're not-- You know, in Auckland bars like that you can just-- Uh, you can just be it out in the open, you know, and I suppose in Palmy you can't as easily. Um, so just to arrive and see that and kind of meet these people that were just really friendly, you know, and-and not judge me into it. I don't know. You know, Palmy often is they're sort of like, "Oh, you've gotta own a car, and soap it up, and drive up and down the Main Street," and I just couldn't give a shit about that, you know, so. Or play rugby and, you know, that didn't interest me at all and sorta come here and have people, you know, talk about interesting stuff and have a good time. I just want to go out and dance and stuff like that. Um, that was quite cool for me to know that that existed because I hadn't seen that before and-and I suppose there's a lot of that that goes on there, you know?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's quite a heavy party scene most weekends and stuff. So it kind of goes hand in hand with that really, and just, you know, I guess when I have-have a slight-- I don't know, you just feel really good, I guess. Just feel, like, happy, and excited, and just to be surrounded by people that, you know, really care about you, and love you and-- Coming from a place where y-you didn't-- don't get that as much, it's just really cool, you know, to-to be able to go, "Okay, on this day I can take this." And it's just that instant, like, "I know- I know I'll feel good." I guess that's part of it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So Auckland, coming to Auckland from Palmerston for you was-was like taking charge of something that you were going to look to make something different in your life?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, in-in a way. Although I wouldn't have been conscious of that really. I just sort of discovered it here. It's not like I came to Auckland looking for that kinda-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -lift to get away from, um, you know parents mainly, and that kind of lifestyle, that Palmy sort of lifestyle. But then yeah, I discovered this other thing, um—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Which you weren't aware of in Palmerston?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. I didn't really know. I guess you see sort of things like that in-in movies from America you know, but you don't really-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: - think that it would exist in your own country. Well, not if you grew up in Palmy.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Palmerston. Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I don't mean to be mean about Palmy but, you know, it's just the different kinda attitude, I guess, kinda- this done-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -to that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like you're ready to move up to something that was different.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And-and you came-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -plus-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -here to Auckland.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. I definitely wanted to get away from something. I didn't know what too, but then I arrived here and found this thing that was like actually, this was obviously, fate or whatever was pulling me to this thing-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -'cause-'cause like I found something in myself or something that was missing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And how does that feel for you now?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, now, I guess, now, I'm just a little used to it. [clears throat] When I first got here, I was like, "Wow, this is amazing." This is hard, I guess, but, you know, it's been three years now, so it's just kinda like I've gotten used to it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, I guess, I'm, let's say I take it for granted but, um, yes, it's just comfortable now. And, um, it's just a sort of what I do really. Yeah, so, I guess that the drugs are linked to that, I suppose. It's j-- Well, it's just a part of it, I don't really think-- I didn't really differentiate it. It's just kinda, "Okay, I'm gonna go hang with my friends," and that sort of thing, you know, that Saturday, Friday night thing. And then it just happens really as part of that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So coming out, feeling-- being gay-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -being part of a gay culture here in Auckland, is feeling good-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And at the same time, it's-it's linked closely with the- with the drug scene with the meth scene for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you're not experiencing where these two things are separate? They just seem to be together more often than not?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I guess, now, that I think about it, maybe it's sort of gone beyond that, maybe I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean like I always-- Well, it's, you know it's kind of a thing that happens in the weekends but, I guess, sometimes in the weekdays. You know, I'll-I'll pretty much every weekend I'll have a big night, um, maybe two but sometimes, you know, in the weekdays like on a Tuesday or Wednesday or something if I just kinda feel like doing something then I might do that sometimes to see if someone else wants to come round and join me or, you know, occasionally by myself I might have a smoke by myself or something like that. And I guess that isn't entirely linked to that scene, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It just sounds like something's worrying you about that there's-there's a part link there but there's not a link and that-that maybe that the drugs is-is becoming a more important part in your life.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm. Maybe. I suppose I hadn't really thought about it-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -until recently.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So something's changed recently?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I suppose just since that kind of intervention thing or I started to give them the benefit of the doubt. And it's-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -maybe noticing some things that I hadn't noticed but—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Tell me about those things you're noticing that you hadn't noticed before.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, I mean, e-even just now, you know, when you asked me how often.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That surprised you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm. S-surprised me to-to think about, you know, when there's stuff, and you don't really think about it, but then if someone asked you, you know, how often or-- and then you kind of have to quantify it, I suppose it kinda sound shocking, you know, if I- if I imagine myself sort of saying, "I do this, you know, a few times a week." It-it-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -sounds shocking. But to me it-it's- it doesn't feel that way, you know, that's kind of where that, where it kind of doesn't sit right. I, [clears throat] that's why I kind of got a bit miffed at my friends a little bit, or I dunno, a bit defensive there. 'Cause you know, it sounds a lot, but it doesn't feel out of control or anything, you know. It doesn't feel, I dunno, people that need to go and see therapists or whatever you kind of go, "Oh, they're an addict." You know. They-- Their health is really bad and they need urgent help right now quickly, Uh, well, at least that's kind of the-the feeling you get. And I don't feel that at all. I don't feel like it's a real urgent thing. So that-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -felt a bit weird.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you're worried a little bit about it and you're going to find out more about it, but you're-you're not gonna take on this notion of being a headache or anything as yet—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So tell me then, um, Ricky, what- what's the other side of the good things that-that using meth or doing some smoking does for you? Is there a downside to it? Are there problems that you're experiencing?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep. Um. Uh, I suppose money is quite a big thing. Like, I used to have a lot more money sorta last year. I had a, quite a good job, like a, quite a regular acting job.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, and it was like quite a lot of money that la-last year. So it wasn't such a problem then. And I suppose I sort of blew that money a little bit. Um, so now I don't have that acting income coming in as frequently and I'm working in a cafe like a sort of part-time and it's not bringing in as much. So now it's kinda like, and sometimes I need to borrow a bit of money or sorta need a bit of help with the rent sometimes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Quite a lot's changed over the last year from—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. A little bit.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It doesn't sound like it was part of the plan.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. But you know, that's the life of an actor, I suppose, ups and downs works and not works.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sure. [chuckling] It's not a secure profession-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and it's-it's hard-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's not.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -it's hard. But is-is there, I just wonder, is there a connection at all between the-the-the-the acting and the meth use in terms of the effect of the meth use on your- on your ability to get work?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm. Could have been a couple of auditions that I didn't do so well and as I could have 'cause of that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: The drug may have had an effect on that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, maybe. Maybe it's just my general sort of state. Um,I dunno, sometimes I suppose just kind of weighs on my mind a little bit like, "What am I doing or why am I spending my money on this?" I mean, when it's happening, it's like, this is amazing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm. Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know am I-- You go in- you go into places, interesting places, but you know, I could just as well have saved that money and actually gone to interesting places I suppose. But I don't know. I wonder if it- if-if it's having an effect. I-I don't know. I can't say for sure, but maybe it's not so good for the face, I dunno. [crosstalk] Dunno if I look tired or-or run down or-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -or if I actually am tired or run down, I suppose. Again, this is things that I haven't really thought about-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -but now I'm starting to think about.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. And they got questions too-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -to ask are they—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're beginning to-to think about those things and-and-and what effect they may have on you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And the choices that you might have about it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What else? Are the-the-the-the problem of around the use of money, you know, the choices that you make around money, and the meth use has taken up quite a lot of the money-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -over the last year and maybe also the effect on-on um, your job and being able-- maybe you're not auditioning as well as you might.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And maybe the effects um, also on-on your physical appearance. An interesting question around the effect of meth use on physical appearance.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, what-- are there any other problems? Any other things that-that are a bit of a downside to this?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, I guess it's obviously having some sort of effect on my friends and my flatmates, 'cause, you know, they set me down and said, "Look you gotta-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -look into this or else we can't hang out anymore."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And that's a problem?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That would be a problem, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: If they didn't wanna hang out, well, then what have I got, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: They're important.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah, and I mean part of it, yeah. Part of it I just wonder 'cause, you know, a lot of those friends that set me down are obviously the ones that are not part of that scene. I mean there were a couple there that-that are, but mostly they were the ones that sort of have always sorta been a bit judgy. You know, like when I first started all this stuff, you know. And clearly, there wasn't a problem like-- 'cause I used to be that guy as well you know, like, "No never do that 'cause it's bad," and then you try it the first time and you go, "Actually, it's not that bad." It's not the end of the world if you're sensible with it, then it's not gonna be, you know.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You have to take a stupid amount to do any kind of like, or, you know, to die or to end up in a hospital.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: YHmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So it's provided you don't-- you're not stupid with it. Then it's just a bit of fun but you can't really explain that to people who are-- have their walls up. So it's hard not to sit in this room full of people kind of going, "Oh, you know, you really should stop the drugs, they're bad." It's like, "Well actually, you don't know what you're talking about."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm. But Ricky, let me just check, 'cause I may got this wrong, just check with you that um, there are some friends that you've got who do use who are still concerned about you. Did I get that right from what you said earlier that-that those who are concerned about you and were part of this intervention some of them use.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep. Yeah, a couple.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you-- So they have their concerns and-and you are beginning to-to ask questions of this use as well and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -it's just that that we're gonna try and drill down a little more into just to pick up for you what-what you think might be going on and what you think might be some of the options for you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And we're g- we're gonna leave labels all that kind of stuff aside 'cause, you know, I'm picking up from you that that's not what that's about.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I'm happy with that. What do you think will happen, what might happen if you can turn your-your uses- you're on now? What-what concerns do you have about not making any kind of change?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well I suppose the acting thing is a really big concern.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: 'Cause I want that to be my job, you know. I'm fucking sick of cafes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: This is gonna be your career. This is the career-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -you want to make.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'd like it to be, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. It's harder when you're trying to create your career, get that going. You gotta- you gotta be at your- at your top, top pitch.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, 'cause I mean it's all you know, it's partly lacking and partly being at the right place at the right time. And if you're at the right place and at the right time and it is not on your game then there could have been a—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, and-and maybe the meth use is-is compromising that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, it could be.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, and then I suppose also like money is linked into that as well, you know, I've-- I'm not doing as many courses and stuff as I used to be doing, 'cause it's, you know, don't have the money.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Alright, so it's back to the money thing again which is-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I mean, obviously I don't wanna keep pissing my flatmates off.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know, and it's not- it's not cool to not pay the rent, obviously. It's not something I'm happy with.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That creates problems?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, and I don't wanna be that person.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Let's just come back to another thing, uh, that we were talking about a little bit earlier, and it's around your meth use as well and-and-and with your gay friends, with gay lifestyle. And-and that sounds like you're saying that-that-that when you party, when you go into the clubs, when you're being with friends that the meth use is always there?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: The-the availability of it is there.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And everyone, most people are using.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Not-not necessarily P or whatever but yeah most people are doing something. Yeah. I suppose yeah it's kind of part of that scene that there's not a huge like, you know, you go to normal bars and most people are just drunk and wasted and like spewing everywhere and stuff and whereas that's a different scene. Like, people drink but they don't drink to that excess but they take other things and have a good time. And, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it might be hard to be part of that scene and not to be using drugs?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean there are people that do that. I suppose it-it would be hard. I-I haven't really thought about it, I suppose. That's all it is, all I've known that scene to be, you know, 'cause I'm quite new to it, you know-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Is it okay if we go over the form you had filled out? We give this out to everybody who comes in.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right. So here, it looks like you wrote that you drank alcohol on a few occasions in the last year, and you have used marijuana more often, 30 days in last year.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. When students and I talk about their substance use, the first thing I always say, I don't like to tell anyone what to do. That's not my job. Instead, I like to see if there's anything they would like to do, if anything, about their use. So what can you tell me about your marijuana use?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, I vape. I have a pen, but I don't smoke it though.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. How often?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, a few times a month.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Do you vape anything else besides marijuana?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I did a peppermint oil once, someone shared it with me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Is it okay if I share some information with you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: We know marijuana has effects on the developing brain. For example, it can make it harder for you to concentrate, it can make it harder for you to remember things, and vaping can seriously hurt your lungs. About one in six people who begin using marijuana as a teenager, later on, become addicted. So what do you think about all this information that I've shared?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it's going to hurt me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How do you think it affects you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I don't know. It makes me relax, and it's fun to laugh with my friend.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Is there anything about marijuana that worries you, many things that you don't like?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to get in trouble like at school.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How could you get in trouble at school?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I can get suspended and I would get kicked off the team, the basketball team.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So staying in school and playing on the basketball team is important to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So when you think about these things, are there any things you would like to change about your marijuana use?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: well, I was thinking to not use when basketball season start.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What would be the benefits of that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I play better when I'm not high.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Marijuana affects how well you play. What would be the other benefits for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't get caught with using a pen, so I wouldn't get kicked off the basketball team.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it sounds like you have a goal of not using marijuana once basketball starts. How long do you think you could not use?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: For about a month.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. If I asked you to pick a number, 0 through 10, 0 meaning you're not very confident at all in meeting your goal, or 10 meaning you're very confident, what number would you pick?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, seven.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: A seven. Why do you think you picked that instead of a lower number like five?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I'm pretty sure, um, I can stop using for a month. I want to play well.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, what steps could you take to help you stop using for a month?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How about this question? What might happen within a month that might make you want to vape?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, if I'm stressed or unhappy, that's when I usually wanna vape.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What else could you do instead of vaping when you feel that way?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm, I like to play video games.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I can play basketball with my friend Sarah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Playing basketball and playing video games are a way to feel better.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad to hear that you have a goal of quitting for a month and you are confident of reaching that goal. If you're willing to come back in a month or so, I would be curious to hear how your plan works out.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, Good luck with basketball practice. If you want anything or need to talk about something before our next appointment, I'm here Monday through Thursday, and it's always good to see you.
