utterances.text: He drives long distance.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And so sometimes he's gone away from home for, what like, days, weeks?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Days, and the longest was, like, a week.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And so he's a truck driver and you are an aspiring social worker, and you have a son who you want to give a really great life to, and you feel that you and your boyfriend are in different, going in different directions-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -maybe? Is-- Can you elaborate on the part that you're maybe the most concerned about or that's the most on your mind right now?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'm concerned that when he was just local, we were able to do picnics and-and-and do the whole family thing that I just really love, and even though my parents weren't together, we would still, you know-- They were really civil with each other and we would go to Disneyland, we'd go to the-the fairs, and you know, I feel like it's different.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Even though I'm not saying that we-we probably won't be together ever, there's a possibility that that could happen, but I still want that togetherness than apart.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, okay. And so that-that realization that you're having right now is, it sounds like, it seems like maybe, just from your nonverbal, that maybe you feel like you need to make some sort of a choice. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah? Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I feel like, um, I'm not, like, valued. We're not valued from his perspective. I mean, that's-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -what I can sense. I can't really make that a final say because he may feel something different.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, you know that he's not physically available-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -to do these things that you want to do-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -like go on picnics.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And so when he is available it's kind of like, I guess where he's at and where I'm at is just like, "Why is that a problem for you?" And I'm like, "It is because I want--"

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: He's saying to you, "why is it a problem?"

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, "why is it a problem?" He feels like it's always me who wants these things and-- but I-I made it clear that, you know, I want our son to grow up with the togetherness-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -especially like how my parents had it, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: They weren't the best of friends but they could come together and, you know, it was better together than apart-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and so I'm feeling like there's a-a change and I don't know whether to roll with it or just accept it, accept it. And it's all a balance between mind and-and heart and that's the battle.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, your heart says you want this great relationship where there's like a true family unit and you can go on picnics and be together but your mind says, what?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, my mind says that it's not going that way and you can't make it turn that way, you can't change anybody, they have to change themselves.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And if they wanted to do it then, you know, it would definitely work.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And I feel like I don't wanna subject to just accepting things the way they are, especially if that's a concern for me-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -as far as dealing with the togetherness, I feel like if I have a problem, I voice it to you and we solve. You know, we'll try to figure out ways so-- I feel like I'm very more like, the collaborating person. Like, we gotta collab together, let's-- you know, I usually am that person that's, "Let's solve this issue."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: "Let's not go over the problem over and over and over."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: "Let's try to think of ways to make it better." And I notice that not everyone's like me in that sense.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And so, do I wanna eventually hurt myself in the long run? Or, you know, help myself by saying, "Okay this is just accepting that he's not in that position, so let me just do what's for me in my heart and, you know-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -stabilize myself to be the best parent that I can be."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so you know what you want, you're not so sure that your boyfriend wants the same thing. His actions indicate that he doesn't.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: His words indicate that he does or he doesn't? You're not sure? I'm not sure about that part either?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm not sure about that part either. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, okay, all right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Because I know that dealing with perspectives you can, you know, you can't really tell someone what their, you know, perspective is-

utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -but I don't-I don't sense it, I don't feel it and, um, I think that's just what I'm going by and I feel like probably 98% true.

utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So now you have this information and it's on your mind, is there-- have you given any thought about what you might want to do about it?

utterances.text: And that's where the sickness comes from.

utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.text: And that's what I'm confused about because, you know, I'm very-- the type of person that, I don't wanna hold things in but yet I don't want to have to keep explaining-

utterances.text: Mm-hmm. [chuckles]

utterances.text: -to you, you know like, I don't want to keep going on, iterating what I want in this relationship-

video_title: Anatomy of a Brief Intervention

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, are you Katie?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Beth. I'm the nurse that works with the nurse practitioner Mrs. Smith that you just saw. Do you have a moment to talk?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, sure. What's this about?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I know you were here to get a prescription for birth control but while you were waiting to see Mrs. Smith, you filled out a healthy habits questionnaire-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and you answered some questions about your marijuana use. Would it be okay if I asked you some questions about how marijuana plays a role in your life?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I notice you use marijuana regularly, and I wanted to ask you more about that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, you know they just decriminalized it in Virginia, it's not a big deal. I'm not in trouble, am I?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: No. No, no, no. Not at all. Um, I just wanted to ask you how it helps you and how you use it. Can you tell me a little more about how you use it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's not a big deal. It's just like a couple times a week to relax.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Marijuana is really useful in your life in helping you relax?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I'm here on an academic scholarship so I have to keep my grades up and I'm on the debate team, so there's a lot going on.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm. You're a very successful student and you have a lot of responsibilities, and it's really adding to your stress.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, yeah. The truth is I'm the first in my family to go to college so I don't know, I guess, I'm in a bit over my head.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm. You've been very successful academically and the transition to college has been hard for you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I've always been an anxious person. Pot just helps me calm my nerves. I'm I in trouble?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I promise you, you're not in trouble, I wanna help.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh, tell me besides helping you relax, what are some positives about pot?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, some of these kids are just so much more sophisticated than me so I guess when I party with them, I feel like I'm fitting in. I don't know how else to explain it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm. Uh, when you use pot in a group you feel more at home with your peers and more accepted?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know if I feel more accepted, more like I'm trying to fit in by using it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So how is it working to help you fit in?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'm not sure it is.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm. So smoking pot with your peers to try to fit in more but it doesn't seem to be making you feel more comfortable with your friends.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What are some downsides to smoking pot?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know. I- It helps me relax but I guess I'm nervous I'll get caught. Um, my parents would kill me if they knew that I smoked.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So smoking pot doesn't help you feel more socially comfortable with your peers and it increases your stress because you're worried about your family and legal consequences?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Can you think of any other downsides to smoking pot?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I don't have the money for it. I just usually bum it off to my roommate, her parents give her a lot of spending money but I don't know, it's kind of embarrassing to have to do that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So smoking pot also reminds you of your financial situation and you don't have extra cash to spend on things?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Katie, it sounds like smoking pot is helping you somewhat in helping you relax and it's also causing you a lot of stress because you're trying to use it to fit in and that's not helping, you're worried about getting caught, you're worried about family disapproval. Having said all that, what do you think you wanna do about your pot use?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know. When you put it that way, it doesn't sound like a very good habit.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Would it be okay if I made a suggestion?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You mentioned at the beginning of our conversation that you have a history of dealing with anxiety, have you ever talked to a counselor about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. We don't do that kind of thing in my family.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Can you tell me more?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's just not done. I don't know. It's something for crazy people and we definitely do not have the money for it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm. So the idea of counseling in your family is for crazy people only and it's looked down upon and the cost would cause a problem too?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I just don't see it happening.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Katie, we know that many kids come to college and have a lot of stress and deal with a lot of anxiety, and we've also found that when they talk to our counselors and learn specific skills about dealing with anxiety, they do much better. Um, and it's been really successful for a lot of kids. Um, I'm wondering if you think it might be helpful for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Can you describe why you're hesitant?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I don't have the money for it so I can't pay for it and my parents wouldn't approve.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, the cost is free and the counseling services we provide, we are legally obligated to protect your privacy. We can't tell your parents. There are some exceptions to that privacy rule, including, uh, mostly if we're concerned about- that your safety.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: What, like suicidal?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, I would never do that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, uh, we can go into some more specifics if you decide to see the counselor about what-what privacy rules there are, but for the most part, you wouldn't need to worry about us sharing anything with your parents.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay. I guess I'll think about it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, uh, if-if you're walking out now, I can walk out with you and just take you around our counseling center. I can even introduce you to one of the counselors.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Do I have to go there?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: No. No, no. I just wanted to show you where it is and let- make sure you know about our resources here at the college.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay, sure. I agree, let's go.

I've been hearing some chatter about a big party that went down and understand you were there. And so I wanted to talk to you a little bit about how partying and alcohol fits in your life right now.

utterances.text: Okay, oh, actually, could I confide something in you that has been bothering me lately. Well, prior to that party, like, as you know, I'm a honor student and my parents, like, they keep me very, like k-kept down out of the, like so- like social life.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, um, about a month ago, my friends invited me to a party. And they used the fact that, Oh, I'm always doing my homework, I'm always studying that to allow me to go to the party. And on-- well, that party, I managed to convince my parents that I would spend the night at my friend's house. So, that's when I started drinking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It was a- it was a unique experience, as you can say. I guess you can say. And, I don't know, I-- It was fun, at least, in the moment. So, I kept doing it. Then this past weekend, instead of studying for an exam, I asked my-- I begged my mom to let me go to another party. And she, kind of, knew what I was doing. She asked me to, like, to promise her of no alcohol, no drugs. Then I'll pick you up by 12:00. And I-I was surprised. 12:00-12:00, that's basically when the party starts, but I told her whatever-- I thought- I thought to myself that I'll-I'll come-- I'll figure out to delay her, can you pick me up later? So later, so she-- I promised that-- She dropped me off, I promised her no alcohol, no nothing. So I-- we go, I have fun like I've been having. And I was drinking. And then the time- the time came for her to pick me up. And as soon-- I couldn't delay her from picking me up. And as soon as she picked me up, and I stepped in the car, she said, "You drank vodka." And I'm like, I-I didn't know what to say. I just looked at the floor. And I-I feel terrible because I-I betrayed my mother. I broke my trust with her that she expected me not to indulge in alcohol. And that's exactly what I did.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, here you are. You're an honors student. You're a star athlete. You've, kind of, been doing everything you've been told for all these years, and maybe last month sometime, you started getting more involved in the party scene.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it was fun at first. But now you're already noticing some consequences.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes, right. Like I've been noticing I've been more lethargic and apathetic towards schoolwork.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I haven't really-- I kind of just sit in class like-- I-- my mind is elsewhere, especially on the weekends, where instead of-- I was- I was instead of studying, I caught up with my friends, trying to find where we can-- I get alcohol based on their age and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It's really changed your focus. What do you like about drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know. It-It's because I'm a very reserved person, for the most part, not when- not when I'm dealing with sports or like-- you know, like a social environment. I tend to keep to myself because I'm very self-conscious, I would say. And when I- when I drink, I feel, I don't know, like, it relaxes me. I'm able to talk or engage with other people more easily. I don't know it just—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, it helps you, kind of, loosen up, feel more relaxed.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sounds like you're noticing quite a few not so good things about alcohol though your mom got mad at you, you're having decreased focus, you're, kind of, not doing so well in school, maybe-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Kind of.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -or any other things?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Just different groups, friends or groups, girlfriends, like different people that I'm hanging out with because certain people are associated with that type of scene.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, that-that-that's also changed.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, your-your friends that you were hanging out with, there's a little tension there now.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: A little bit because not all of them are into that. So, like, I'm in one group of friends, and I would talk to another person that's an another group of friends and they just happen to invite me to that first party.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, since then, I've been hanging out more with them, getting to know them. But I can also see that oh, I'm just living life, I guess. But that's also not fair to them that I'm not there for them as much as I was before.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: As they are there for me, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, given that you've sort of noticed all these changes where it's affecting your friendships, it's affecting your studying, it's affecting your relationship with your mom. Where do you think you should kind of go from here?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, um, I feel I should st-stop. I mean, like, I'm not-not unrealistic. I understand that situations like this will happen.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's just up to me not to take it so far, where I can't remember the night before, if I'm puking. All I remember is the toilet-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -that's-that's not worth it, either. And I have to slowly build back my trust with my mother because that was that's a big blow. It's little so I guess may seem to other people.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But to me then it's a big thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Your mom is really important to you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And how she feels about you is important to you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How important is it to you to make, uh, an adjustment in your drinking or even to quit?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: A lot at this point because I feel that's a big factor with gaining back my trust with my mother.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And also getting back on top of my school work again my athletics too.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So I feel that there-there's a future in that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How confident are you that you could actually change your drinking or-or even cut down or quit?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'm pretty confident, especially.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: O-on a scale of 1 to 10 where one is not at all 10 is completely what number would you give.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Probably like an 8 or 9.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And that can't be a ten there's nothing as ten in life I feel. Like there's too many factors but I feel like I'm determined to.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Why did you say eight or nine rather than six or seven?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Because I don't know I feel deter-determined to-to make sure this happens because I don't like how I felt after I-I betrayed my mother. I don't like remembering that the feeling of like vomiting.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's not a pleasant experience. Uh, it's not something that I wish to enjoy. So like even if I do drink, I don't want to drink to the point where that happens, like all the fun that I have and prior to that just it's not worth-it's not worth drinking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right, what do you think's a realistic goal for you then?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: To make sure I have my studies. Well first, try to get-get back my trust with mother-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -then just focus on my studies. Then if I have time for leisure time like I'll go party with my friends and just be as a party with them doesn't mean I have to drink. And I do one cup is not going to do anything to my life either. But I'd prefer not to do that. I prefer just make sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So your goal is kind of to do not drink at all or if you are at a party, uh, a maximum of one at the very most.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Exactly. Just so I take part with the social convention but it's not. Hey guys.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Chris, I really appreciate you talking with me about this. I know it seems like something that's been on your mind as it is and, you know, like I said I really care about you as a student and an athlete and want what's best for you. So I'm glad we were able to talk about this. It really seems like you have a good plan going forward, you know, really striving for not drinking alcohol at all and if you find yourself in a situation where there's alcohol, making sure to have that limit of one drink maximum. It sounds like something that will work for you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And-and thank you for listening me listening to me. It means a lot to me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It's my-- yeah it's my pleasure. It's part of my job and it's probably like this so. I'm going to hurry up and get changed for practice.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, Sandra.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Thanks for coming in and talking with me for a couple of minutes. I understand you don't have very much time, but I really appreciate you stopping by.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I came today because my daughter's in the hospital as well. I think it's important to quit, but I enjoy smoking. I'm not ready to give it up right now. My life is too much in turmoil.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So I get the impression that there are some things that you're concerned about, but that overall, coming in here wasn't necessarily the first thing that was on your mind when you came to the hospital with your daughter. Um, so can you tell me, what was it that made it possible for you to even come in? What-what were some of the things you were thinking about?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think it's important because I've-- I feel I'm a bad role model for my children, and my daughter's turning 12, and already, some of her friends have tried smoking, so I don't want her to think it's a good thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So the last thing you'd want is for your daughter to start smoking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I smoked when I was young, and I certainly don't want it for her.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm. And it sounds like your smoking, setting an example, those are some things that-that you're also, uh, a bit concerned about, um, but as you said earlier, not-not really ready to put down your cigarettes immediately.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, that's true. It seems so hard. I'm just not ready for this right now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So Sandra, what's good about smoking? What do you like about it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's very enjoyable, relaxing, you know, a stress reliever. When I'm at work, we all go out and smoke and chit chat and, you know, talk about things. I would hate to not smoke, really. I'd be left out.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What else? Tell me what else is good about it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm, I like to have a cigarette after I eat. It sort of tells my brain I'm finished, stop eating, I'm full. So it's a- it's a way to-- you know, sometimes I'll have a cigarette instead of a snack, so it's a way to control my weight.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So is there anything else that you like about it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Let me think. Well, I just enjoy it. I think it's, uh-- it's not good for me, I know, but I'm so used to smoking. I don't really think about quitting too much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So let me make sure that I understand all of the good things about smoking, the things that you like about it, and let me know if I've missed anything or left anything out.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So it sounds like it's a way to relax. It's a way to socialize with your friends from work, and it's hard to imagine what it would be like for you at work if you couldn't go outside and smoke.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That's true. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You also mentioned that smoking is a way to manage your weight, and concern that if you were-were going to quit smoking, what that would do in terms of, um, gaining weight, and that smoking after meals is pleasurable, that it's something that would be really hard to give up.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I also heard that it's very much a part of your life. It's something that you've done for a really long time and almost impossible to think about yourself as a non-smoker. Does that capture, for you, some of the good things or things that are keeping you smoking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So I'm hearing there are some things you really like about smoking. What about the other side? Can you tell me about some of the not-so-good things?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I-I'm worried about my children. I feel like I'm being a bad parent, and um, I often wonder, you know, they've seen me smoke for years. I certainly don't want my 12-year-old daughter to start smoking, and some of her friends are already smoking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sandra, can you give me an example of a time that you did something that you think left an impression on your daughter or set a bad example for her?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, just this morning, I was outside having a cigarette, and then when I looked up, there she was looking out the window watching me smoke.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So this morning, that experience, it really brought home how she does watch you, and she does really look up to you and notice what you do. How did that feel when you looked up and saw her watching you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I felt terrible, you know, I was projecting-- I wanna be a good parent, and I don't feel this really is part of the plan.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And again, thanks for your honesty in talking about this. I appreciate that this is a- this is a tough topic. This is a-a hard behavior to think about giving up. Um, I guess one thing that- one thing that doesn't make sense to me is that, you know, on the one hand, you talk about how being a good parent is your highest priority, it's really important to you to set a good example for your daughter-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -um, and on the other hand, I'm hearing you say that smoking is important in terms of stress relief, socializing, and it's something you can't imagine ever changing. How do those two things fit together?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It doesn't fit, you know. It's the opposite side of the coin. You know, I love to do it, but I don't think it's right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So what would it take for quitting or changing your smoking to be something that was more important, that raised it up in the list of priorities for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I can't think of anything right now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't have any plans to quit. It's just something I'm thinking about.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, it's-it's not so much that you don't wanna quit in a way, it's almost, "How could I do it that would work for me?"

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. I appreciate. We've- we've probably used up the time that we have. I would love to see you next week if you'd be willing to schedule another appointment and talk with you more about this. Is that something that would be helpful?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, sure. Sure, I'll come in. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So I hear-- [crosstalk]

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: We can talk about it some more.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: [chuckles] Not necessarily the-the most exciting thing for you to do, but I appreciate you are willing to do that. Can I also ask you to do a little bit of homework between now and next week? I promise it's not too time-consuming. Um, we have a booklet that we like to give folks who are just thinking about changing, who aren't sure that this is something that they're ready to do, and one of the exercises is to write down your top three reasons for change, why you would even consider quitting smoking. And then to reflect on some of the good things as we talked about, as well as some of the less good things about quitting and about continuing to smoke. Is that something you'd be willing to do over the next few days?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay, okay, I'll give it a try.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, here you go.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So thanks for coming in, Sandra. We'll see you next week.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text:
In what ways might your life be better if you succeed in 
making the changes you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's pretty cool that you did that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I felt proud of myself.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You should be proud of yourself, and how did you do that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I was just like thinking of like when I'm- whenever I like I'm saying like stuff back, mom gets really mad at me, she's like, "Well, I'm not gonna help you anymore." 'Cause, she tells me to like leave it be, but I really don't lis-listen to her so she gets mad. So I tried like thinking of like her feelings and like what would happen after if I say, "This is lame, leave me alone," 'cause then they'll like stop and I won't get like yelled at anymore.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh, that says a lot about you and your mom's relationship though that you can kind of put yourself in her head and think about how she would feel about it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You know what I mean? It's pretty cool, not everybody can do that, so. So you could kind of put yourself ahead, uh, it's almost like watching a movie ahead-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and knowing how it's gonna turn out.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: 'Cause usually, if I get in trouble, mom gives me the silent treatment that I don't like. It's like she doesn't talk to me, I'm like trying to talk to her, she don't like wheezing being like, uh, I don't like it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's the worst, the silent treatment.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, so, um, so but that worked for you, where you just let it go, you thought about your mom, you like what we would call like, you channeled to your mom, you know, and, uh, channeling mom, and then, um, you were able to walk away, and you were proud of yourself and nothing bad happened.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Does it--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like they all like stopped talking to me, and the funny thing was that their eighth-graders that like didn't even go to my old school like I don't even know how they said of talking to me, I was like, creepy.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, so- and so when you- when somebody else told you that they or people said you that you're an easy target, um.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, they don't really say that to me like I just like think that 'cause that's what I've like heard from my mom, and people talking to me 'cause I keep talking to them-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -so they keep coming back at me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so they-they kinda know how to hook you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and reel you in-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -right, and get you upset. And then bad things happen and then you get in trouble.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. [chuckles] That happens a lot.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So, yeah. And it's, uh-- So, um-- so you-you know that when you're kind of channeling your mom, that helps. It sounds like you taught yourself almost. Like there's-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -a conversation inside. What other ideas do you have about what you could do?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I was thinking of like, um, if I'm like at school like a peep things are happening during class-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -I just say, can I use the washroom or something to go like walk and like think of like how to like leave them be. And one time during my gym class, there's this girl that I had her like not talking early. And we're playing pickleball, I don't know if you know that, it's like a-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I don't know what pickleball is.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -it's like a badminton, big life-size ping pong ball game.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It looks like a pickleball?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, you have like a big bracket—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: There's no pickle?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, [chuckles] there's no pick.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I wanted to pickle and stuff.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. And like I was supposed to be like again turn. I told my-- I went to my gym teacher like silently and said I can't be by this person, can I move to the next court. So he like switched us around so I won't be by her. And that like happened.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's a really good decision.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: The girls like what the heck like.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. No, but how smart on your part to know that if you would- if you would had to play with her, something bad would've happened.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Like I would like smacked her in the face or some- [laughs]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You knew that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -or something.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right? You knew that. So-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you know actually which kids-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, that's like—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -know how to push your buttons that real you in.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, there's like four main ones but not that like I can say who.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's okay. That's-- Yeah, 'cause it's not important. The important thing is for you to be happy. And, uh--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And the friends that I have like I know are my true friends, They're like ones that don't really 'cause drama or like—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, they might but like they're not like bad and they actually like help me. Like some of these girls that like so-called friends like-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -They're like they come to me saying like, "Oh, did you really have to like punch this girl." I'm like, "No." It's like you're not a friend if you'd actually believe that, you know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, it's kind of annoying, 'cause it's kind of hard like going into high school and like knowing how to believe and who not to believe.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. That's-- that-- it's-it's really big unknown territory. Pressure High School class is probably 1,000 kids.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: 1,003 kids.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And then there's the sophomores also that you have like another 1,000, so it's like—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -potential enemies, friends, who knows which ones.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, with these like the first rumors had started going around about like my friend and I, and like I lost him just 'cause of rumors. It's like, what the heck. Like I couldn't get over him for like gosh, who knows, it was like three months and I finally just had got over him.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That must have been hard for you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I was like really, you're probably just jealous 'cause I was friends with him or something.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So but finally after three months, time went by-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and you got--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just found like other people and just like forgot about it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And so how else do you identify who your friends are that you can really trust who have your back?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I say the ones that like not even that I've known the longest, but like the ones that actually hang out with me a lot, or like texting me a lot, or like calling. And the ones that are actually like that helped you before with like situations. And that they tell you stuff and they know they can trust you. Like one of my friends tells me everything about her. And like that's how I know she's a good friend 'cause she trusts me with things.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You trust her back then?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that makes a lot of sense that people-- it goes both ways.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You know. And, um-- So and for you, friends that, um, kind of, um, give you the attention that you'd like to have. Texting you-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -calling and you hanging out with you, and stuff like that, rather than pretending to be a friend-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -when you know maybe they're gonna--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, that happens a lot with me with like a lot of friends. Like this one person like we've been friends since like-- Well, we were friends since fourth grade.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And like she just starts like lying and like just talking smack about me. And it's like, you're not a good friend then. Like I thought you were a friend since you've been my friend since our fourth grade.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And she just like causes a lot of drama now. And like she came- Like the friends I met at high school, she came like into them like, you're not gonna know-- In college, you're not gonna know who to follow 'cause-- since you keep following with my friends, what are you gonna do in college like not being able to find your own friends? It's kind of annoying 'cause they're my friends and like I can't be by her and she comes to my friends. It's like-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -get your own friends, [chuckles] stop following me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Wh-what don't you like about her?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: She just lies a lot and like just starts dramas about me and I haven't even talked to her like since eight grade. We only went to school together and she just like makes me lose other friends 'cause of the drama she starts

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So she sounds like she's, um--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: A nobody. I'm gonna say that. She's like—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Or-or not worth your time.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: She's not worth your time. So what would it be like for you to really just spend time with the friends that you know are really--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I do spend time with them. Like I hang out with them a lot.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Good. That's really good. Yeah. And if-if you need like some extra support from them--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Ask for it. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right, and what kind of things do you ask from them?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just ask them like if I'm like gonna get like sent down to the principal's office for like something happening, I call them to come down to, like, support my, like, backup information.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: 'Cause they can do that. They can- they can kinda give you some, uh, information like, uh, um-- they can give some accurate information, um, and back up your story versus the other person's story.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, okay. So we're-- You know what? Um, it sounds like you actually have some pretty good ideas about, um, how to handle this, and yet kids are-- I know kids-- actually, adults can be really mean too. But, um, I know in high school, i-it's really bad.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So I'm wondering if, um, uh, if-if you wanted to, we could get together again and continue to talk 'cause you-you've got some good ideas already. And I'm very open that if you wanted to bring any of your good friends in, that that would also be totally cool too.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So would that be something--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, there's one friend that might wanna like talk about it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And she's really like-- she doesn't know, like, who to talk 'cause her mom is not always there for her.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And so like she's like doesn't know where to go.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like she doesn't know who to believe.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, I would want this session though to be for you though, Molly.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I mean I'm willing to see her too, you know.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like she really needs-- she'd like someone to listen to her.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So, um, we could maybe talk about some other ways of, um, helping, uh, deal with this because, um, it does sound like, um, people are, you know, just being plain old mean to you for no good darn reason.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And, um, so you'd be willing to come back and talk about it then? Okay. All right. And I just wanna let you know that I think that you're, um, really doing a good job of-of, uh, dealing with how hard it is to be in high school, 'cause it is hard.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I've noticed that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And it is hard, and-and I-I think it gets better. My experience was it got a little better. The freshman and sophomore year, you know.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: But, um, anyway, I think you are hanging in there beautifully, and I love hearing that you're involved in swimming and some other things 'cause they must help connect you up with some pretty-- I would hope-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -[unintelligible 00:13:12] people. So okay, anything else? No? Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hello, nice to meet you again. And, uh, and what seems to be the-the problem or what-what prompted you to come along?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, just I'm sick of my drinking. I'm drinking too much. Um, I just thought, uh, maybe I need someone to talk to, get some help about it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so you feel as if drinking is a problem for you at the moment?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, it's just- it's just got worse over the last six months?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Wh-What makes you say that it's gotten worse?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I guess, I drank, you know, like most people do before, um, but I broke up with my boyfriend, uh, about a year ago and then six months ago I guess I wanted to go out again and see if I can meet people.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And I've been, yeah, getting into this habit of going out every Friday and Saturday, now, uh, drinking a lot.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, to try to meet guys.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, uh, in the last few months I've been, you know, just drinking even more on week nights, and I never even used to do that before.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, okay, so you've noticed over, I guess, uh, the last six months in particular since you decided, you know what? I'm going to take a risk and-a-and go out to try to meet a-a-a pot-potential partner again that it's with an increase in drinking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, I just, I don't feel comfortable talking to guys normally. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know what to say, um, and I just, drinking helps.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sure, sure. So you're noticing that the drinking at the moment is a way of perhaps calming the nerves?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, for sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: To-to-to speak to-to potential partners?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Who-who-who, boys?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, I guess, like most people do when they go out they drink.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I've been doing that and just drinking more and more I guess.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, and it's just-- it's not even working, I'm not really meeting people and I just end up with massive hangover for the rest of the weekend and—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's interesting isn't it? You-- 'cause you kind of mentioned it there, like, you know, on one side of the coin, um, it helps calm the nerves to get yourself get out there and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -talk to guys at the same time, on the other side it's not working you're finding. And i-i-it results in hangovers or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, I've maybe talked to people but it's just, uh, that I've just I think I'm just too-too drunk and I just, my friends drive me home and just the end of the night I don't-- yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, and so I guess, you know, what would you like to do given the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I guess I just wanna stop. I just feel like I'm drinking more and more 'cause I'm doing it now in the weekdays-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and I mean, I just don't-- I don't wanna do that every now and now I just think it's a bit too much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm just I'm not eating properly anymore, I'm just eating less or just getting takeaway, getting crap food and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -um, I'm just, I feel like I'm not exerc-- well I'm not exercising like I used to. So, I just wanna cut, you know, stop drinking so much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, okay, so, uh, sounds like you really want to stop drinking, particularly during the weekdays?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah I do. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right, because you're noticing it's having a negative impact on what you're eating.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I don't wanna- I don't wanna, I mean, I don't wanna stop altogether, so.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: No, I get it. Yeah. I mean, you know, it sounds like it's, it is helpful to a degree for you when you go out because it makes you feel a little bit more calm to talk to-to guys is that right?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah and just and all my friends go out and drink. Like I-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -I'd have no social life if I didn't.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: If I just said-said, "No, I'm not drinking at all," and, you know, I don't feel like I'm an alcoholic-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -or I don't feel like I need to

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. So, you've got, you know, some benefits there then, you know. The social element, hanging with friends and-and going out together is something which is-is quite enjoyable. So, it's not a case of removing it completely but it’s a case of, "Okay, I’m noticing this is impacting on me more than what I’d like to." Yeah. Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, it just got a bit out of control.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Has there been times in the past where you’ve tried to cut back on drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, this hasn’t happened before.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, this is the first time anything like this has come up?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, due to just circumstance of, I mean, I just yeah, had my boyfriend for six years before that and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, before that yeah just my friends weren't drinking so much, and yeah it’s just not, it's just new. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, yeah. Well, it’s great that you’re able to identify, you know, what’s going on at the moment and you've-- not only know that, you almost picked up on a bit of a pattern too you're in-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -as to why you’re-you're drinking. In terms of looking at cutting back on-on drinking, you know, on a scale of 0 to 100 and 100, uh, meaning it’s tremendously important for you and 0 not important at all. How important is it for you to cut back on the drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I believe 80, I mean I guess that’s why I’m here so—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, yeah yeah sure, you're already taking a huge step forward in many ways by coming along to-to start talking about it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, I guess 80 is quite high, what makes you say an 80 over say 50?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I don’t know, I just-just I don’t know, it just sort-- it just got up to a point where just, um, it seemed just too much, like no-nobody else is really drinking as much in the week as well and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -it seemed, as just, yeah, for the reasons I was saying, just seeing like I need to do something about it now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, yes, so you’ve got this real sense of, "I've gotta do something."

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Just seeing it’s just gonna get worse, uh, wha-- that’s what it seems like.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That’s what it seems like.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, at the moment, it's been a case of the last six months, this is a pattern that you’ve been noticing more and more, um, a sign that it has had negative impacts on your lifestyle which you’re not happy with and you are in you're in a position where, you know what? I wanna do something about it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, I mean what do you think that next step is?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I guess that’s why I’m here. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Just to, uh, but um-- I is-is-- I think the weekdays is what I really need to do.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, and then, I don’t know, try to plan it out a little bit more on the weekends-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -so it just doesn’t go crazy.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, okay, so you’re thinking about perhaps looking at trying to keep weekdays free of alcohol? Was that what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, how does that sound like a first step goal for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, that’s good, that’s-that's, yeah, that's- that is definitely what I’m gonna do.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just, you know, I'm so out of the routine, not exercising, I need to get back into things.
