utterances.text: To be frank, Mark, I honestly don't know. I mean, I honestly don't know what causes it because I've never had any reason. It came upon me from the GP and it took me back.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, the hereditary thing I thought, well, maybe that's the explanation.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That makes a bit of sense.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And why go any further, it's there?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Can't help it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: They live pretty long lives, they did, all right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: They managed with it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Relatives relatively went into their 70s.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. I don't know if it'd be helpful for you if you'd like to know a little bit more about some of the factors involved in time Type II diabetes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: If that would help.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: If there's something that you think that-- Yes. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, I'll perhaps share with you what I know from working with other people and some of the things I've experienced in working with people.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And see what you make of it. See if it fits a little bit more with where you're at. We know that there is a strong family factor or hereditary factor, so that's one aspect. So also it tends to happen a little bit later in life, rather than something you might get when you're a teenager, this type of diabetes. So-so it's a later onset. It takes a bit of time for it to develop maybe. And the main reason I think, um, the main aspect of it is that it, have you heard about insulin.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I've heard of it yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So that's a hormone or a chemical, it allows you to utilize sugar in your body.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right. And Type II diabetes typically people have a resistance or a resistance to insulin in their cells, in their fat cells or their muscle cells or liver cells. They can't use insulin. And so sugar builds up in your system.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Are you saying that they-they like they can't digest insulin or is that?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You need insulin in your cells, individual cells in muscle or in fat or wherever to, um, use up excess sugar or to utilize sugar.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So-so it's like a-it's like a balance.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So insulin you-you.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Kind of, as your.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You have yourself draws bar.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yap.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Or something, and then what balances that out in the body is the insulin taking off the excess.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Or-or digesting? Should I say the excessive sugars?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's a good way to think.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Exactly. And what's happening in Type II diabetes is your-your fat cells and liver cells and muscle cells are resistant to insulin. It's almost like they're saying we can't use that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And if-- Well, there's a number of-- We're not entirely sure, there's a lot of research still going on as to how this happens and how that could be modified. But what we do know is that, um, one of the key things in managing it is to try and modify or modulate, control the amount of sugar that are in your system.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So there's a couple of things that we know that people with Type II diabetes have to look after and have to think about if they want to control the amount of sugar that's in their system, which is the main issue that's causing some of the health problems that people have with Type II diabetes. Too much sugar, and if it's not able to be utilized in the blood cell, in the fat cells, or liver cells, and the muscle cells stays in your bloodstream. And that can cause problems with your circulation. So too high blood sugar and too low a blood sugar can be a problem. So sugar is the main concern in Type II- Type II diabetes.And you mentioned earlier on, a couple of things that the doctor-- You've mentioned some signs that he was kind of a little bit concerned about. Well, what things did you notice over the-over the last month or so?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You mean, personally?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know. I mean, the thing is you see that-- I mean, I did think about this a little bit and I thought, well, over time, if things happen slowly, you don't really notice.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: As you get older.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, I don't-I don't leap over five bar gates like I used to, you know, um, as opposed to, uh, running with the backs now, I tend to spend more time, you know, with my old mates in the bar.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: At the rugby club and-and-and the such like, yeah. And, um, the fish I'm hooking, I'm not after the kings anymore, I go for the snapper now, it's a bit easier, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: A slightly more sedate lifestyle.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, absolutely. You just do.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You just do. Um, so you're less demanding, I guess, on your-on your body, you realize, and you don't really want to do these things anyway. You know, you let the youngsters get home.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Been there, done that. So you don't really notice. So I'm coming back to this diagnosis I had from my GP and him saying, "You've got diabetes 2," well, I should feel like that, shouldn't I?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. It should feel like there's something really wrong with you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What's-how have you been feeling over the last month? So, you say you're very busy you're doing a lot of work.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean I'm a busy person. All right? I uh, my work uh, I work in insurance, so I'm always hopping from one place to another place.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I haven't noticed.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mh-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I really haven't noticed how, um, okay I get a bit--I suppose I get a bit out of breath sometimes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: If I rush too much that-that's true. Um, I suppose, um, I don't go upstairs two at a time anymore, I use one at a time.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So a little bit sort of energy is not quite there sometimes? The vitality.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, certainly the energy I have is-is not what I-what I had. I mean I do need to, you know, I'm busy but I do need to sit down, um, uh, I do need to sit down and relax with a cup of coffee, you know, and, uh, things.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, Mh-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, more than I would normally.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But that would be, that would be about it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mh-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, is it getting worse? I don't know. I-I-I suppose. What worse? Is it-is it increasing? Well, to say, I don't really notice it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You haven't noticed it. So it's a progressive, you know, you've just seen this, as-as you got older, things have slowed down. You know those activities you used to do, but that's kind of like what happens.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. Um, at least, that's what I think. I mean I don't know if you're telling me that I should be more active or my GP is saying I should be more active.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mh-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, as I say, uh, you know I-I don't do any regular form of exercise, I have to say, not anymore.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But maybe I-maybe I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm, a bit of a mystery there.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean I've got uh, well I-I mean I've got a great lifestyle. I mean if it's very-it-it's very good. I mean I've got all my mates in down at the rugby club. And I've got uh, you know even in the summer when that's a bit damn. I used to coach rugby and I coached cricket when I finished playing. So-so I've got the-the guys in the cricket club, um, you know, for the-for the, uh, for the summer evenings. And, uh, and then, uh, the-then, of course, we've got the fishing, and that's all of us combined. We're a big gang, really.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Really? So what I'm hearing is there's actually a lot of aspects in your life which are really good.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, I think my life yeah. My life is great.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: From your perspective, things are going well?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: My life is great, and then you turn around and say, "Hey you've got-- you-you're ill, you're sick.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. It doesn't fit.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And um, no I'm not. But you see, he said to me that he's gonna put me on some sort of, uh, a daily monitoring of, is it sugar levels?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mh-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And I'm gonna have to take regular pills.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well frankly, the only pills I take are sort of paracetamols.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. When you get uh, a headache.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: For a bit of the head in the morning, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So the idea of having to test-test your blood sugar and take medications is kinda like off--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Come on, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you know that's a bit too-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, life is too short.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Too much.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know it's the truth.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean you know—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you're here today and that's probably something in you you've thought well I'll follow this through, you know I'll-I'll come along and see what-see what they've got to say. And I'm just wondering for this session, for the time we have today, there's a number of things we could talk about. You mentioned a couple of things about your lifestyle and, um, medication is one thing you've been told by the doctor you might need to do that. And a number of things that we could talk about today. Which-which area would you think would be useful for you to focus on?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well there is-there is something that you sort of prompted me to think about, and, um, I split up-- My wife and I, we split up several years ago now. And, um, you know we've been married for many many years.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And um, I think she used to look after me because she used to do the cooking and-and-and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And I have to say that I'm not the best cook in the world.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mh-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, and-and being on the run all the time and you know once I get back home, it's, you know, it's time to go down to the rugby club or whatever it might be, uh, we're out with the mates. And, uh, I-I do I suppose my food is not as healthy perhaps as it used to be when she was around. She's moved down to Hamilton to live with her mother, if you've met her mother. Anyway, but, um.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So then, since you've been on your own since you've separated, divorced and you've noticed that the things you eat and how you eat has changed.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean mates and their wives are pretty cool about it sometimes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Because, you know, they'll invite me for dinner and so on.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, yeah, yeah, yeah. I guess, you know, that's when you, well, or whatever reason, you split up in life.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You start looking at the home life of somebody else, you're thinking, "Hmm, I use d to have this."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm. Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And you think, " This is nice food, " isn't it? and you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And your-- part of your wife used to do a lot of that for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, she would do all the cooking. Yeah, yeah,

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, I never bothered to boil an egg in the water, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And so she would kinda look after what you ate and healthy things that you had, spread in front of you and off you go.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Totally. I mean, I was just in charge of the wine, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. And now you have to think about what you might eat and sometimes you don't eat the best.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well I-- This is what I'm saying. Maybe I'm not thinking about it. Maybe that's the thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe I'm just—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know, because it-- you know this-- the pizza shop's just on the road.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And then there's-- I mean, okay, I confess that lunchtime, occasionally, it's uh, I'm hungry and McDonald's is very convenient

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -or Kentucky Fried or whatever.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Very appealing, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know, it's very easy. and then, um, then you think to yourself, well-- I mean, I do think of myself that maybe I should have a few vegetables around here or whatever. But then you go out into the supermarkets, you know, and you can pick up, uh, your- one of your TV dinners.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So you bring those in and you open them up and put them in the microwave and there's vegetables there.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah they look pretty good on the plate, don't they?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, it looks- it looks fine, you know, et cetera. I mean, so that will happen occasionally if I've got a night in. But cooking-wise, no, I haven't cooked anything, um, other than boil the water for the kettle for a cup o coffee.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -for ages.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: They're food choices in what you eat and what's in your diet it's not what-something you actually you've actually been aware of or had to think about in the past.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I do miss her breakfast. I have to say, we used to have get a nice breakfast.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So one thing that you noticed is diet and the eating patterns and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -when you eat. That's one aspect. What other aspects do you think you've-- you would be--?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I used to be quite a heavy smoker, right? I mean, I'd smoke a pack in a half a day. And I knew that wasn't doing me any good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean the thing is when you're a-- I mean, I've always smoked. So, but when you're young and you're a sportsman, you know—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You kinda juggle those two things and kinda--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, the two things they balance out, you know and everybody else is

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You still run and have a cigarette?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know, you pass a cigarette down the backline almost, don't you? You know, just before the game gets—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm. Hmm. Yeah, part of the culture.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, part of the of the whole thing. And it's changed a bit now, because in my day when we were playing, of course, it was a very much more of a social game, which was spent-spent in the rugby club.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That's why you played and it was a big buddy-buddy thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That was rugby and cricket was the same really.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, but now—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: But over the years, you've actually reduced your smoking or you've stopped altogether or at times?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well I-I, yeah. I was getting a bit sort of-- I was getting a bit, you know, a bit wheezy and I thought, "I'll cut this out."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But I enjoy smoking. I really do enjoy it. So I cut it down to I suppose it's about 10 a day now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so you meant to reduce.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You were noticing that it's having an impact on your breathing and health wasn't so good.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: When you related that to your smoking, so you managed to reduce your smoking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. I sort of—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you've made our decision to do that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: it-it-it's-- you know, she will, "Why don't you give up? You've gone so far, why don't you just stop?" But I don't want to.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's-it's-- I-I enjoy it, um—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, and it's hard to get to stop something you enjoy, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, yeah. I mean, you know, the thing is that you get to, you know, you've got to-- when you get down to that, you, uh, you have to regulate sort of-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know, you have to be quite strong-willed about, I suppose, in a way.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So you say, "Okay, well, you don't have a cigarette unless you have a cup of coffee. [laughs]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Of course, that's a double-edged sword a bit, because then I found I was drinking more coffee, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: But they go together so well. And sugar in the coffee?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, yeah. I have two sugars. A couple of sugar in coffee. Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So we cut that down as I say.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But the problem goes that coffee, we're up to 8 or so, 10 cups of coffee a day now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're drinking more coffee. So what I've heard you say so far is, if I can just start right back from the beginning and you used to come in and sais, "I went to the doctor." You went for-- it sounds like you went for just a checkup.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, you know, there's a friend of mine, one of the guys down the rugby club, he said- he said, "I'm going for my annual, you know-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: MIT.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -warranty of fitness, sort of thing, you know. And I thought, now that's an idea, not been to one of those.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Got to check out, why not?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So I'm 55, and you read in the papers, you know, it's that at 55 you will-- you know, heart disease is more prevalent

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and all these sorts of things that you get around this middle-age time. So I thought, "Well, I'll go and have one." And frankly, when I went along, I was very confident. I thought, you know, the doctor is going to saying, "Hmm, I wish I was as healthy as you," sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, but unfortunately, uh, he-he came up with this. And it's the only thing I think he really came up with. I think-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So everything else looked pretty good?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: My cholesterol is quite good, not too bad.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Cholesterol good, your weight is good.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah-yeah. Not too bad.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, you are smoking, but you've managed to reduce that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I've cut it down, yeah. I mean, that's been three years, mind.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And anything else, you know, you go ticking down the list. The tire is good, oil good.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So we're looking good.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And then we come to this-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And ah, hang on.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -too much sugar in the tank, or something. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, there's something wrong with the, uh, with this bit.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it doesn't quite fit with how you see your own lifestyle.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Because you've-- it sounds like what you've been doing, you've made some conscious effort to be aware of some of those things you might think are important.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, yeah. I mean, you know, the thing is, you see, the thing is, and I mean, and probably you've-- I think you've heard this before, but people, they turn around, oh, uh, you know, doom and gloom prophets, you shouldn't drink.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You shouldn't smoke.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And then I think to myself, "Well, maybe I shouldn't socialize." And then after that, "Well, maybe I shouldn't be alive."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So like a domino effect, and they'll all be just sitting-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know. I mean, what-what-what's going on here? This is- this is- this is so many people's lives.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And um, I suppose, you know, if it came down to it, then, and somebody said, "Well, you can solve this problem by taking a pill once a day, um, you know, it will keep it down, and there will be no problems," Then I-I could go with that. But what I don't want to do, um, the doctor was saying, or insinuating, that I'd have to change my lifestyle.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: A bit broad kind of like you've gotta change everything.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. It was um, and I-I said, well, no. I'm sorry. [coughs] I'm not going to change my lifestyle. I've got to where I am. I'm reasonably happy. Okay, I wish I wasn't separated. Okay, I wish my kids were-were still around, um, you know. One of them is off now in, um, in-- back in Europe playing rugby in France.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And your thought was, yeah, right, I hear that, but actually, I don't want to make all these big changes in my life.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, I don't want to, because I don't feel that I need to.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Feel like you need to. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, it's you know, why?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I can't argue with a medical professional, Mark, because I know nothing, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: The test, is the test, and experience, yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, I mean, what-what-what-what suggestions would you have? I mean, what-what sort of-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I don't know. I think it's up to you where we start, and that's the question I've got in my mind. You've mentioned a couple of things that you've already made some effort, or been conscious of. You've mentioned the diet, you've mentioned your smoking, those are two quite important aspects that we often talk about here in how people work.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Is smoking related to diabetes then?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It can have an impact, yes. So smoking, um, affects your blood system, so it hardens the arteries, um, and over time, it can have a significant impact on the healing of wounds. So people with Type II diabetes, often, if they get a cut, or a bruise, or something, it takes a long time to heal. Smoking reduces the amount of oxygen in your system, so that can further, you know, limit the time it takes your body to heal.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So we know that smoking and Type II diabetes together-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Don't help.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -isn't a good combination.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Is it okay if you have one without the other? I'm sorry, it's a silly question. [laughs]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, the question is, I suppose, that I have for you is, where would you think, for you, would be a good place to start? If you were gonna make any changes, even small changes at the beginning, rather than just thinking, oh, I got to change everything, which it sounds like you're not prepared to, you know, do a whole lifestyle change, and I don't think that's what we're talking about here. Where would you feel most comfortable to start if you were gonna make any changes at all?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Where would I start? Well, I-- What if about if I cut down on sugar in the coffee? If we could have long blacks, no milk, and no sugar.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Hmm, that might be a start.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think I could- I think I could probably handle that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hm. What we also find is that people make these little changes, small changes, and that starts to kind of well, it makes them-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Something of a rollover effect.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -rollover, the domino effect starts to happen, and they start looking at other aspects.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Domino effect, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So rather than thinking, "oh, my God, I have to change all these things. I've gotta stop smoking, I've gotta exercise more, I've gotta, you know, start eating more fruit and vegetables," you might start with these small changes, and then-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, how much exercise should I do a week?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, I-I'm reluctant to give a prescription for that because I think it's really up to you. And I think it depends on how things go, as to how much you need to do.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier on, the doctors talking about you monitoring your blood sugar.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So on how-- It depends on how-how that goes. Let's say, if you started doing that and you do some more exercise, you start to have longer blacks, rather than short blacks with lots of sugar. And you get down the sugar and you find your blood sugar starts to come down, then we're heading in the right direction.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay, so—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So it's really, I suppose, up to how things go for you, and you get that feedback. And if that's going in the right direction, you carry on doing and do some more of that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, a-are we saying then that-that, really all I need to do, for this moment, is I can forget about everything, but cut out the sugar, uh, in the coffee and the milk-- I don't know, but you might as well, you know, milk without sugar is silly. But, um, if we do that, is that where we start?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I think where we start is where you feel comfortable starting.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I mean that's something that's not difficult to do.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Apples for breakfast.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You start off at breakfast and get yourself an apple, a bit-a bit of apple and-and so on. Um—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So what I'm hearing you're kind of saying is, that there's-- You're now starting to think of some very useful little starting points.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Not huge changes, but some little things you could do.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it's kind of dawning on you there may be some possibilities here for making some changes. Let me ask you this. Um, let's say you put some of these things in place and you start to make some of these small changes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, where do you see that taking you in the next set of three, four, five years? You know, where do you want to be in three to four years' time? What would be your ideal picture?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, you know, and this is difficult because I don't feel unhealthy now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, I suppose it would be fun to-- Maybe I should join a club or two, that's what I'm thinking because I'll be with mates.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah? You like the social aspect?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I love the social aspect of it, and, um, there's-there's-- I know there's a bar in this club as well. I-- Don't-don't misunderstand me, I don't drink-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: No, no, I get that. I get that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -till-- You know, I'm not an alcoholic or anything like that, I—

utterances.text: So part of that whole keeping fit and exercise stuff is actually the social side of it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, and then—

utterances.text: You can see some benefits and some enjoyment that.

utterances.text: That sounds like a great plan.

utterances.text: And so maybe that would, uh—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, sounds like a good idea.

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I think anything you do, it has to be something you've decided. You know, just start where you want to start. utterances.text: Those are some really good ideas and good starting points. So thinking about it like that, what-- Where are you now? What's your-- What-what-- Where-where is your thinking now?

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think to myself, I think, "Oh," I think go—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Quite invigorated with the idea of--

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, this is- this is- this is cool, it's like an old challenge again.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Making some of these changes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: This is good. And, um—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're up for the challenge?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Modified and looked at, to get the best out of ourselves, to get the best out of the opportunities we have.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think you're- I think you're right. I think, um-- And again, you put them together and it's-it's-it's becoming-- It's-it's a sort of a-an individual team job, isn't it really?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That, okay, do a bit of this and do a bit of that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Some good things I'm- some things I'm good at and there are some other aspects we think, "Well--"

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, but I don't have to give up anything really, do I?

utterances.text: It's not about giving up your personality or-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No it's not. It's not.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It's just tweaking things. Just fine-tuning a few areas and being a bit more aw-aware of one aspect of your life a bit more, like the food choices or whatever. Well, Mike, I-I've really enjoyed listening to your perspective, and your story a little bit, and it's helped me a lot to get an idea about where you're coming from, and a little bit about who you are, and what's happened in your past. And-and we've also talked a bit about what's going to happen next. And you've come up with some great ideas. What I hear you saying is that, you know, before all this, before you met the GP, things are going fine.Well, as you would of-- As, you know, as you'd seen it, you were just doing your thing, and getting on working, and being busy, and being successful, and then suddenly this diagnosis, this doctor tells you that you've got a problem.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It comes along to me and talk today a bit about how you felt about that. Initially, it can be quite a bit of a-bit of a shock. It didn't quite fit with how you saw things.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: True, true.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And as we've been talking, I'm hearing you're saying that maybe if you look back to where you were before you went to the doctor, things weren't quite that right, maybe. Things weren't as good as you thought they were.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, you see—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What you're kind of thinking about what those might.

utterances.text: Alcohol can have some dangerous effects on your body. So along with contributing to high blood pressure, it can have a big impact on your liver, which you need to keep in mind. utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: In summary, the Minnesota State, Mankato security report states that you were stopped on Stadium Road last Friday, cited for driving under the influence, and then you were transported to detox. Plus, you're only 21 years old. Is the report accurate?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I-I guess, uh, I don't really remember much. I like it was a week ago, so I was kind of drunk too.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Behavior like this could get you suspended, doesn't that concern you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm. I mean, not really. I'm gonna be 21 in a couple of months. Um, once I turn 21, the cops can't give me a minor and I mean, I'm not a heavy drinker, like-like my friends or anything. I don't get wasted at all. And, uh, I just need to be careful. I just won't get caught. I'm just trying to find, like, a normal college student.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What were you thinking when you got into your car after having six beers, you could have caused an accident and killed somebody.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Whatever, I-I didn't though. I called my roommates for a ride. He was sleepy. So I had to get home somehow. And this isn't even my fault. I give him rides all the time, but I didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You need to take responsibility for your actions. If you keep partying like this, your problems will only get worse. You're likely to face costly legal citations, poor grades, health problems. Getting kicked out of school and disappointing your parents. You don't want that to happen, do you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No-no. Like I said, this isn't even my fault. Like, are we done here? I have class in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Your behavior is not what Minnesota State University expects of its students. If you wanna be a student here, you'll need to show that you're able to follow our rules. Do you think you can do that, otherwise, you'll be suspended?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Look, I really like going on the [unintelligible 00:02:29] and I get what you're saying. You, you're making some really good points and I'll think about them. Okay?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, your sanction is you'll be placed on university disciplinary probation and you'll have to attend an alcohol education seminar that'll cost you $150. Also, disciplinary action is progressive and cumulative, meaning that any further violations will result in suspension for one semester or longer.

video_title: Stop smoking - initial consultation

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Good morning. It's really nice that you've come along to see me to talk about stopping smoking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What have you got in mind, what do you want from us?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I need some medication if you can offer me some.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Absolutely, we're in the right place for that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, uh, whatever else you can do just to get me to go smoke-free.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just remind me again why it is you want to stop.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's, uh, just these days-- I think these days I'm-I'm finding that, um, I'm smoking 20, 30 a day, I'm getting sick of it. It's, you know, I've seen my friends have stopped smoking too and it's kind of they're looking at me weird these days like I'm the only one left who's still smoking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, good, and so feeling under pressure here.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Especially the other night I was at the restaurant, it was a bit-- you know, it was a bit embarrassing I'm the only one walk walking out.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And so that-that can't feel a little uncomfortable being by yourself. So that sounds like one of the reasons you have to quit is it's a little getting smelly and it's getting embarrassing.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Any other reasons?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, it's expensive these days.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How much does it actually cost you a week?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's-it's about-- Um, I'll buy and go through a pack a day, so it's almost £7.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: £7 a week or a day?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: £7 a day today, so-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So your pack a day—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -you're talking about £40, uh—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: £50 a week.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: £50 a week.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Even more mess, you see.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So we're talking about spending £50 a week-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -being one of the few left smoking in your crowd, and not liking the smell. That sounds like three reasons.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Do you think that's enough to make you say goodbye to cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great, okay. So have you got a date in mind when you'd like to stop smoking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, what you do-- What do you suggest?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Generally, it works well if you find a time when you're not under a huge amount of other stresses and strains.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What are the main reasons why you actually smoke? What do you enjoy most about it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, it's just entertainment. Something, um, when I bored, it's got-- I've got-- I smoke-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -or sometimes I go out, but as I said, I'm the only one kind of outside.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What do you think you'll miss most about it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: The-- Um, it takes away a lot of my stresses.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, what sort of stresses?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Just, uh, when I- when I go down, uh, for-for a break at work.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I never go down, I just need a break away from it all, just shut off. So, uh, I-I really enjoyed that. The cigarette just helps me calm down.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And what is your favorite cigarette of the day?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's definitely the one at the end of the evening.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so the end of the day-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -the thing that helps you just unwind, put an end to the work section and move into your own time.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So after you've had the quit date, what do you think you might do when it it's the first day at work and it's time to go home if you're not gonna have a cigarette?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I guess, um, I'll just- I'll just have, you know, some fresh air as well, but this time without a cigarette in my hand but to try and give myself regular breaks maybe, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's one of those tough things.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Have you managed to stop smoking in the past?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I've managed for a couple of weeks.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And what got you back?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It was, um-- To be honest, it was stress from an argument with my partner I remember.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So something just happened-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -so it took you back into it. All right. Let me just make sure I've understood what's going on here. You really want to stop smoking because you're kind of the last guy in your group still smoking, it costs a lot of money, and you don't really like the smell.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: The main reason that you smoke is because, at the end of the day, it gives you a kind of relaxation, and if there's quite a little stress that's going on which you're using cigarettes to help you cope with.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What you'd like to do is stop and you'd like to sort of like choose a time to quit when it's going to be there's not as much stress around as possible. When do you think would be a good time for you to choose to be your quit date?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I guess, um, at the weekend I've got a party coming up.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, uh, maybe Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So Monday morning after the party will be a good day, and that's next week. Okay. Now, one of the things that we do in the pharmacy is recommend that you use medication to help you. You know this increases your chance of success and it makes it more likely that can manage any cravings that come along. A lot of people like using nicotine replacement therapy which comes in a variety of formats like patches, gum, you've probably seen people using any of these products. And other options are tablets which you can get from the GP.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, yeah, again-- Um, so have you something in mind that you might like to use to help you through managing the cravings?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm thinking, um, one of these patches.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So a patch is something you've already seen, and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and, again, I'll get some out and I'll show you what they look like. This course of medication lasts for 10 to 12 weeks. And we strongly recommend that people stay on the whole course of medication and that that gives you the best chance of success. Stopping smoking is not easy but it's possible and with the type of support that we offer here in the pharmacy, you absolutely make your chance of success four times greater than trying on your own, so, that's why it's really good that you've come to see me. Now, what you said is you really want to do it and that next week sounds like a good day for you to start because the party is over and done with.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You've got the time at the end of the day when you finish work, which might be the first time you've gone without a cigarette. So, what I'd like to recommend is that you use two products perhaps and I'm thinking of you're having a patch and then suggesting that you might use something that you can top up with. Often, a person who smokes knows exactly what it feels like when they're craving for a cigarette. What does it feel like to you, when you can't have a cigarette and you want one?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just get irritable.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And that's exactly one of the symptoms of nicotine withdrawal that I'm looking to stop happening to you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, I would strongly recommend that you have the patch. I'll talk to you about how to use that and that we have another product that I leave you to use as when any of those feelings of irritation are coming up, particularly in that first week.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you're happy with the date for [unintelligible 00:06:16]?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay and would you like to come back and see me again?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And what would you like me to do if you don't come back?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: A nice phone call.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I'd be very happy to do that.
